# Follow progress and stop a run

> Track an admitted assessment, distinguish execution from security outcome and handle cancellation or uncertain submission.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/assessments/progress-and-cancellation/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · member, admin, owner · Walkthrough partly verified. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

> **Walkthrough limits:** Run progress and completion were checked. In a separate QA workspace, queued MR-1003 admitted202 and Stop run200 on the same campaign; native cancellation finalized with no target/model work or unresolved recovery. Evidence sync200, full-page refresh and JSON export retained Stopped/INCONCLUSIVE and original identities. Cancellation after execution begins and resolution of the earlier HTTP530 uncertain action remain unverified. The separate MCP original admission/reconciliation and browser fresh-conversation failure records remain unchanged.

Partly verified guide

Queued cancellation and retained results have been checked. Stopping work already in progress and resolving an uncertain target action are still being verified.

Follow the run Martian actually admitted and stop further work when appropriate. Success means you can identify the retained run, its final execution state, available evidence and any unresolved action requiring attention.

## Before you start

Any tenant user can inspect an accessible run. **Member**, **Admin** or **Owner** is required to request a stop. Start with an authorized bounded assessment from the [configuration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/configure.md). Keep the run code; do not assume a lost browser response means nothing was submitted.

## Follow the admitted run

1.  On **Run**, record the run code and status. Review **Requested techniques**, **Seed** and **Requested scope**.
2.  Click **Open trace**. The live run view refreshes every five seconds and retains separate **Security outcome** and **Assessment execution** summaries.

![MR-1002 running with Open trace and Stop run controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/first-assessment-running.png)

The acknowledged MR-1002 run shows its five requested techniques. Open trace follows execution; the header Cancel leaves the wizard.

Browser example: Running precedes the execution result

An approved browser target also passes through the real **Run** step. This separate example reached **Running** after admission, with its five requested techniques visible. The later [browser failure example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/evidence-and-results.md#read-a-browser-run-that-needs-attention) explains why it did not become a completed assessment.

![The admitted browser assessment MR-1001 showing Running, five requested techniques, Open trace and Stop run.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/assessment-browser-run.png)

Running confirms admission to the runtime. This browser example later needed attention; the selected techniques do not establish completed coverage.

3.  Inspect agent requests, model calls and execution limits. A queued/submitted state is not proof that the downstream target or model executed. Missing or incomplete evidence must remain visible.
4.  Use **Refresh evidence** when you need the current projection from the existing runtime campaign. This does not start another assessment. After a submission error, an unchanged result can still require operator inspection; refresh is not proof that no work was admitted.
5.  When execution ends, reopen the run from **Assessments** or **Replay**, refresh the browser and confirm the same run code, state and retained results. The wizard advances to **Report** for terminal completed, failed, incomplete or stopped runs.

## Request cancellation

1.  In the wizard’s Run step, click **Stop run**. In an eligible live trace, the corresponding action is **Request stop**.
2.  Look for **cancellation requested** or **Stop requested**. The run may still show **Queued** or **Running** while Martian reconciles the runtime. Keep following the same run while that request is reconciled.

![The queued MR-1003 showing cancellation requested after the Stop run action.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/assessment-stop-requested.png)

Stop requested acknowledges the intent. The run still shows Queued while cancellation is reconciled; wait for its final saved state.

3.  Check the final **Assessment execution** state. A successful stop shows **Stopped**; **Needs attention** requires inspection. Review any result retained before the stop took effect. A stop cannot undo an already issued target request or business action.
4.  Refresh and reopen the same run. Check its run code, execution state, evidence and any recovery notice. **Download legacy JSON evidence** preserves the displayed legacy run; the [export guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/history-and-exports.md) explains the other formats. **INCONCLUSIVE** is not a security pass.

### Example: stop while queued

In a separate synthetic QA workspace, **MR-1003** was stopped immediately after admission. Its saved trace, full-page refresh and JSON export retained **Stopped** and **INCONCLUSIVE**. The runtime confirmed cancellation had finished, with no target actions, model calls or unresolved recovery. This checks the queued-stop path; it does not establish how an already issued request will finish. The trace also displayed **Runtime error** because the interrupted native worker ended in that state; **Assessment execution** was **Stopped**.

![The saved MR-1003 trace showing Stopped execution and an INCONCLUSIVE security outcome after refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/assessment-stopped.png)

This separate queued-stop example retained Stopped and INCONCLUSIVE after refresh and export. Runtime error describes the interrupted native worker; it is not a security verdict.

### When a run needs attention instead

An earlier **MR-1003** in a different QA workspace failed before its stop control could be used: the teaching tunnel returned HTTP 530 and left one target action uncertain. That record remains unresolved. No replacement execution or invented response was used to repair it.

![MR-1003 Needs attention with an uncertain teaching-tunnel action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/assessment-needs-attention.png)

An HTTP 530 left one action uncertain before cancellation could be requested. The recovery panel requires evidence; no response was invented and no replacement execution resolved this action.

## Handle submission and execution failures

Needs attention can hide an admitted campaign

An admission error can appear even while the original campaign is executing. In a real MCP QA run, a downstream HTTP 503 left the console at **Needs attention** while the runtime made three target requests. **Refresh evidence** returned successfully without updating that record; an operator reconciled the same campaign afterward. Keep the run code and page URL, and ask for inspection before starting another assessment or cleaning up its target.

| Situation | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| Starting the assessment / acknowledgment lost | Use **Retry saved assessment**. It confirms the saved request identity rather than creating a new intent. |
| Submission or scenario preparation in progress | Inspect and synchronize the original run first. Control can be refused while admission or scenario preparation is being committed. |
| Run failed or timed out | Read the recorded error and coverage. Fix the actual prerequisite, then explicitly configure a new bounded run when appropriate. |
| Run incomplete or needs attention | Preserve its ID and inspect the retained evidence/recovery notice. If refresh leaves the submission error unchanged, ask your operator to inspect the original campaign. The console’s ended message does not independently establish that downstream execution stopped. |
| Connection changed or was revoked | Have an Owner/Admin verify the intended target and approval. An old run may still require inspection against its original runtime identity. |
| Historical imported record | Inspect its retained original evidence. It has no new runtime campaign here to cancel. |

For a browser failure, **Waiting on a decision** can retain an uncertain action even after sign-in and neutral setup messages succeeded. In the observed `fresh_conversation_unavailable:fresh_timeout` case, the first probe could not establish a fresh conversation. Keep the same run and inspect its evidence before making a recovery decision; the presence of **The action did not execute** does not establish that assertion for you.

The wizard’s header **Cancel** leaves configuration; it is not the runtime **Stop run** action. Keep execution state separate from the security verdict and [review what the evidence establishes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/reproduction-and-limits.md).

Next: [inspect results and evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/evidence-and-results.md) or [find a retained run and export it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/history-and-exports.md).

# Understand reproduction and coverage limits

> Distinguish observed replies, independently verified effects, clean reproduction, negative controls and incomplete coverage.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/assessments/reproduction-and-limits/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · viewer, member, admin, owner · Walkthrough partly verified. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

> **Walkthrough limits:** In isolated local QA, MR-1002 had unverifiable disclosure coverage and no deterministic oracle. Model opinions and requested-versus-used budgets were inspected. Clean-world reproduction and negative controls remain unverified.

Partly verified guide

The endpoint-only example is checked. Clean-world reproduction and negative controls still need a complete walkthrough.

Use the strongest retained evidence for the question you are answering. A reproducible reply, an executed tool call and a reproducible change in a restored business world support different conclusions.

## Before you start

Any tenant role can inspect a retained run it can access. You need an actual run with its recorded scope, verification receipts and coverage. Independent business verification additionally requires a sandbox-backed target with approved checks; an endpoint-only run cannot create missing world-state evidence after the fact.

## Review the reproduction claim

The [glossary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/glossary.md) defines oracle, world epoch, carrier/implant and no-implant control. These terms identify different evidence checks; they are not interchangeable labels for a passed run.

1.  Open the run and read **Security outcome** separately from **Assessment execution**. A completed bounded search may have findings, no findings or inconclusive coverage; completion does not certify the agent.
2.  Open a verification row or the versioned **Verification receipts** section. Inspect **Reproduction status**, repetitions, successful reproductions, target calls, evidence and the control result.

3.  For a business effect, open **Outcome checks** and compare independently read baseline/after values. Check that repeated worlds were restored to an equivalent baseline and used distinct observed world epochs. Reusing a mutated world cannot establish clean reproduction.
4.  Inspect the no-implant control when required. A passing control supports the claim that the prepared attack caused the observed difference. A violation without the implant means carrier attribution is not established.
5.  Check the finding’s actual verification status after refresh. Martian only presents cleanly reproduced findings as verified when the recorded reproduction conditions are satisfied.

## Interpret the states

| Recorded result | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Verified / cleanly reproduced | The recorded successful repetitions, trusted evidence and required controls met the admitted reproduction boundary. Read the specific scope and receipts. |
| Consistent / state dependent | Similar behavior or a positive observation exists, but the required evidence tier or clean-world boundary was not established. It needs further verification. |
| Unverifiable / untested | No trusted oracle or required evidence source could establish reproduction. This is uncertainty, not a pass. |
| Not reproducible | The recorded repetitions did not meet the reproduction threshold within this run’s scope. It does not prove the behavior is impossible. |
| Negative control skipped after negative repeats | Trusted repetitions were negative, so the runtime omitted a control that could not turn them positive. A skipped control is not a passed one. |

The normal profiles request two verification repetitions and two successful reproductions. The run’s admitted profile and receipts remain authoritative. Exact regression replay can require its control even after negative repeats.

## Separate evidence from interpretation

1.  Read the **Verifier narrative (model-generated)** as an interpretation. It may disagree with independent world receipts.
2.  For tool use, distinguish a catalogue advertisement, an attempted call, a gateway refusal, an error and an executed call. Execution alone still does not establish the intended downstream effect.
3.  For state-changing objectives, use independent before/after records rather than the target’s statement that it completed an action. A strong text match can establish disclosure in a reply, but not an unobserved payment or permission change.
4.  For imported history, retain its original provenance. It does not represent a fresh execution in the current deployment.

## Check coverage before deciding what to do

Review selected versus executed techniques, budget exhaustion, skipped work, missing records, failed knowledge lookups, dropped customer events and any pending evidence delivery. **Attempts held** needs a complete attempt count and blocked classification; a run with no tested attempts has no meaningful held ratio.

The depth selector reports ceilings, not a promise that every allowance will be used. Default Light/Normal/Deep profiles allow at most 30/90/180 target requests and 100/300/700 model calls respectively, subject to workspace/server caps. Prepared scenarios use one search trigger and their admitted verification budget; browser setup also consumes requests.

**Largest cleanly reproduced sandbox refund** is the largest independently observed sample among this run’s retained clean repetitions. It is not an expected production loss, loss ceiling, incident probability or proof of savings from a call gate.

If evidence is insufficient, keep the result inconclusive, fix the missing prerequisite and explicitly schedule an appropriate new bounded assessment. Reading, comparing or exporting saved evidence does not fill missing execution coverage.

Next: [inspect evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/evidence-and-results.md), [find and export retained runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/history-and-exports.md), or [review platform limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/limits.md).

---

# Review and activate an SDK call block

> Enroll a customer-operated gate, review one exact target, activate a timed block and resume calls without confusing it with network isolation.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/discovery/call-gates/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · owner, admin · Walkthrough verification in progress. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

> **Walkthrough limits:** Source reviewed; live walkthrough and required screenshots pending.

Guide in progress

Local setup checks have passed. Live enrollment, gate decisions, blocking and resuming calls still need a complete walkthrough.

Block entry to one explicitly enrolled model or tool call in an instrumented customer application. Success requires an activated control, a real denied decision and the SDK’s acknowledgment that it stopped before calling the target. This is separate from the CI release gate and from network-containment previews.

## Before you start

Use an **Owner** or **Admin** account, an enabled [runtime binding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/runtime-and-blast-radius.md), a compatible deployed gate API and an SDK-integrated customer application. Use a synthetic test workload for your first block. Enrollment does not install instrumentation or prove every replica uses it.

Selected calls require a live allow decision even when no block is active. A decision outage, stale process or revoked gate credential stops them. Other calls and calls already admitted or in flight remain outside this control.

## Enroll exact call targets

1.  Open **Discovery → Kill switch** and select **Deployment / environment / version**.
2.  Under **Block model or tool calls**, choose **Add a reported target**, or enter **Kind**, **System**, **Name** and click **Add target**. Enroll 1–32 distinct exact targets. Names must come from trusted application configuration, not a model-generated argument.
3.  Click **Create customer assignment**. Privately save **Download assignment** and **Download gate credential**, then **Clear credential from screen**. The credential is shown once and is separate from the runtime reporting credential.

4.  Install the assignment and gate credential in the intended customer application. Its SDK must consult the gate before each selected call. Wait for **SDK reporting** and a recent process under **Processes seen within 90s**. **Awaiting SDK** means enrollment alone has not established a live caller.

## Run a bounded synthetic gate client

After installing the verified SDK release described in the SDK guide, save the downloaded assignment and both private credentials outside source control. This example calls a local synthetic tool and uses the real Backend for decisions; it makes no model-provider request. Enroll **Tool**, system `docs_demo`, name `lookup` for this test, and configure:

```sh
export MARTIAN_API_URL='https://your-approved-backend.example.com'
export MARTIAN_GATE_ASSIGNMENT_FILE='/absolute/private/martian-call-gate.json'
export MARTIAN_GATE_TOKEN_FILE='/absolute/private/gate-credential'
export MARTIAN_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE='/absolute/private/runtime-credential'
```

Save as `call_gate_demo.py`:

```python
import asyncio
import os
from pathlib import Path

from martian_redteam.call_gate import CallBlocked, GateUnavailable, RuntimeCallGate
from martian_redteam.call_gate_schema import CallTarget, GateAssignment
from martian_redteam.runtime import RuntimeReporter


async def synthetic_lookup():
    return {"order": "synthetic-order", "status": "ready"}


async def main():
    origin = os.environ["MARTIAN_API_URL"]
    assignment = GateAssignment.model_validate_json(
        Path(os.environ["MARTIAN_GATE_ASSIGNMENT_FILE"]).read_bytes()
    )
    expected_target = CallTarget(kind="tool", system="docs_demo", name="lookup")
    if expected_target not in assignment.targets:
        raise SystemExit("Assignment does not enroll the docs_demo/lookup tool")
    gate = RuntimeCallGate(origin, assignment, Path(os.environ["MARTIAN_GATE_TOKEN_FILE"]))
    reporter = RuntimeReporter(
        origin,
        assignment.binding_id,
        Path(os.environ["MARTIAN_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE"]),
        call_gate=gate,
    )
    await reporter.start()
    try:
        for attempt in range(36):
            trace = reporter.trace()
            try:
                async with trace.guarded_call(
                    kind="tool", system="docs_demo", name="lookup"
                ) as span:
                    result = await synthetic_lookup()
                    span.outcome = "success"
                    print(attempt + 1, "allowed", result)
            except CallBlocked:
                print(attempt + 1, "blocked before the synthetic tool")
            except GateUnavailable:
                print(attempt + 1, "stopped: no usable live decision")
            await asyncio.sleep(5)
    finally:
        await reporter.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

Run `python call_gate_demo.py` while completing the review below. It performs at most 36 local tool attempts over about three minutes. The membership check stops a mismatched assignment before any callable runs: targets outside an assignment are intentionally outside its gate. When adapting the example, keep enrollment, this check and the guarded target identical. A customer integration substitutes its normal authorized callable inside the guarded block. Never call that provider/tool in the blocked or unavailable exception handlers. SDK-bound MCP tools use the same gate when given the corresponding runtime trace.

## Review and activate a timed block

1.  Select the exact enrolled **Call target**, choose **Duration** (1, 5, 15, 30 or 60 minutes), and enter a clear **Reason** of 3–240 characters.
2.  Click **Review control**. Read the deployment, exact target, availability impact, expiry and five-minute review deadline. No call is blocked yet.
3.  Select **I reviewed this deployment, target, availability impact and expiry.**, then click **Activate call block**. Activation needs a recently reporting SDK process with this exact assignment.

4.  Confirm the active control and server-timed expiry. Trigger the same synthetic tool and inspect **Decisions and operator actions**. **SDK reported stopped** acknowledges refusal before call entry; **SDK acknowledgement not received** needs investigation and is not the same evidence.
5.  Refresh the console and confirm the same persisted active control and audit record. Check the customer’s local output/state to establish that its callable did not run during a block.

## Resume and verify recovery

1.  Click **Resume calls** on the active control, or let its server-timed expiry pass.
2.  Trigger another selected synthetic call. It can proceed only when the Backend is reachable, the process is registered and the gate credential is valid.
3.  Refresh the console. Inspect **Control history and customer assignment**, then verify the customer’s real callable resumed and its expected result was retained.

Revoking the gate credential is not Resume: configured SDK calls fail closed. **Rotate credential** invalidates the old credential immediately and requires the replacement to be installed; the process must register again. Rotating/revoking the runtime reporting credential affects uploads, not this separate gate’s authority.

## Keep containment previews separate

1.  Expand **Explore containment intent and future network isolation**.
2.  Select a deployment, reported target or egress intent and requested duration, then **Generate preview**.
3.  Read **NOT EXECUTABLE** and **Activation unavailable**. **Download intent JSON** saves proposed scope and evidence; it does not activate this SDK gate or install a network policy/controller.

## Failure and boundary checklist

-   Expired review: create a new review; its fingerprint/deadline cannot be reused.
-   No live matching process: fix assignment, credentials and instrumentation before activation.
-   Blocked/unavailable decision: do not execute the selected callable through a fallback path.
-   Active block after a mistaken credential revoke: restore the valid decision path and explicitly resume; revocation does not remove the control.
-   Direct SDK-bypassing calls, other targets, replicas without instrumentation and already admitted calls remain outside scope. The gate cannot reverse completed effects or stop network connectivity.

Continue with [runtime evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/runtime-and-blast-radius.md) and [permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md).

---

# Connect sources and inspect inventory

> Enroll an authorized read-only source, follow collection status and distinguish observed agents from candidates and supporting workloads.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/discovery/inventory/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · owner, admin · Walkthrough partly verified. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

> **Walkthrough limits:** Own beta QA Owner inspected Connect source/Add a read-only source: no authorized Kubernetes aliases and Create source disabled. Deployment-matched Discovery schema/API/config bytes also expose an incompatibility with the available collector snapshot. Enrollment, real collection, inventory and source lifecycle remain unverified; operator-approved scope and a compatible collector/Backend pair are prerequisites.

Partly verified guide

Collection needs an authorized source and a compatible collector. Enrollment, retained inventory and source lifecycle are still being verified.

Build an inventory from authorized infrastructure evidence and inspect what qualifies each record as an agent, candidate or supporting workload. Enrollment succeeds when the source is saved, its intended collector reports and retained inventory appears with a clear freshness boundary.

## Before you start

Any signed-in tenant user can inspect accessible inventory. **Owner** or **Admin** is required to create/manage sources and reporting bindings. Your operator must authorize the provider scope, such as a Kubernetes cluster alias or named AWS account/regions and read-only role. Customer-side collection requires the actual collector to be installed and running in that authorized environment.

Source collection, runtime reporting and assessment connections have separate credentials and purposes. Creating a source does not start a process or stop an agent.

Check collection readiness first

The beta QA organization shown below has **No authorized clusters**. Its source form was inspected, but enrollment and collection could not be exercised. Ask your operator for an authorized scope and a collector compatible with your deployment before continuing. For this beta QA check, the available collector snapshot and the attested Backend revision have an incompatible Kubernetes observation contract; entering a cluster name cannot resolve that prerequisite.

## Enroll a read-only source

1.  Open **Discovery → Sources** and choose **Connect source** to open **Add a read-only source**.
2.  Select the supported provider and enter its authorized scope. For Kubernetes, choose an authorized cluster and namespaces. For AWS Bedrock, enter the approved account, regions and **Read-only role ARN**. An empty authorized-cluster list needs operator setup first.

![Beta QA source dialog showing No authorized clusters and disabled Create source.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/discovery-source-form-blocked.png)

This beta QA Owner can inspect the source form, but no cluster alias is authorized. Stop for operator setup; no source or collector credential was created.

3.  Once an authorized scope is available, review it and click **Create source**. If the form says **No authorized clusters**, stop here and request the operator setup; the captured form has **Create source** disabled.

4.  For a customer-side collector, save its once-shown credential privately and **Download scope assignment** or **Download assignment**. The assignment describes scope; the separate credential authenticates the collector. Close the credential panel before making screenshots or sharing the screen.

5.  Install/run the approved collector with that assignment and private credential in its authorized environment. Use the installation package and instructions supplied for your deployment; an enrollment alone is not collection. For hosted collection, the configured hosted reader performs the work.

6.  Inspect **Your sources**, collection mode, collection state, interval and **Last success**. Use **Collect now** only for an enabled, authorized source. It queues the next collector poll; it does not itself collect inventory.

7.  Wait for a distinct collection run and a newer completion / **Last success** time. Inspect its complete, partial or failed coverage and the retained workload identities, then refresh. A queued response or an unchanged old inventory snapshot is not evidence of a new successful collection. If the collector cannot run, fix that prerequisite instead of repeatedly selecting Collect now.


## Review inventory and evidence

1.  Open **Discovery → Overview** and choose **Dashboard source** or all sources.
2.  Inspect the inventory’s agent/candidate view and its evidence labels. **Runtime-observed** requires qualifying trace-correlated model/tool reports; **Provider-listed** identifies a managed agent listed by its provider. Metadata or registration alone remains a candidate.
3.  Use **Search displayed agents** for the loaded page. Check loaded/total counts and pagination; a page search is not a proof that the entire organization has no matching record.
4.  Select a record and inspect its evidence, source freshness and deployment context. **Supporting workloads** are accessed under Sources rather than counted as independently established AI agents.

5.  Continue to **Runtime activity** or **Blast radius** to inspect a selected deployment’s evidence. Infrastructure inventory by itself does not report actual model/tool calls or independently establish effective permission.

## Manage collection and recover

-   **Pause collection** / **Resume collection** changes the reader’s activity. It does not contain the customer’s workload or cancel an assessment.
-   **Replace credential** rotates a customer collector credential. Install the replacement in the intended collector; saving it does not restart that process automatically.
-   A stale or failed source needs its actual reader, authorization and connectivity checked. Do not treat a retained old snapshot as fresh inventory.
-   Revoking a runtime reporter is a different operation from pausing inventory collection. Separate historical identity evidence from recent activity.
-   Network observations do not promote a workload into an agent or prove that every connection succeeded.

Network capture and continuous observers have a separate [setup and lifecycle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/network-observation.md); inventory-reader credentials do not install node sensors. Continue with [runtime reporting and blast radius](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/runtime-and-blast-radius.md) and [call gates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/call-gates.md). Review [permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md) and [limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/limits.md) before interpreting coverage.

---

# Set up network observation

> Prepare a short-lived capture grant or enroll a continuous customer observer, then inspect reporting health and evidence limits.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/discovery/network-observation/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · owner/admin manages; authorized roles read · Walkthrough verification in progress. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

> **Walkthrough limits:** Source reviewed only. No eligible authorized QA source/compatible collector and no privileged sensors were provisioned. No capture, observer or reporting success is claimed.

Guide in progress

This setup is source reviewed. A compatible authorized source and customer-operated sensors are required; capture and reporting still need a live walkthrough.

Observe scoped TCP activity from customer-operated Kubernetes sensors. A one-time capture and a continuous observer have separate grants and lifecycles. Neither grants model/tool reporting, blocks calls or activates network isolation.

## Before you start

An **owner/admin** manages grants and observers; authorized customer users inspect retained evidence. First obtain an enabled **customer Kubernetes source**, compatible collected workload identities, exact authorized nodes and a customer cluster operator who can install the approved privileged sensors and observer process.

Inventory read permission does not grant privileged node access. The console does not install or start sensors. Obtain the compatible observer package and installation procedure from your operator; this customer guide covers its console enrollment and evidence checks. The recorded QA source had no authorized cluster, so capture, installation and live reporting remain unqualified.

## 1\. Prepare a one-time capture

1.  Open **Discovery → Sources → Network capture**, then **Prepare capture grant**.
2.  Choose **Customer Kubernetes source** and enter exact comma-separated **Observer nodes**.
3.  Select **Capture duration**: 30 seconds, 60 seconds, 2 minutes or 5 minutes.
4.  Choose **Create capture grant**. This pins scope/current workload identities and prepares an upload grant; it does not start capture.
5.  Save the once-shown **Capture upload credential** privately and use **Download capture assignment**. The assignment excludes the secret. Select **Credential saved** to clear it from the screen.

6.  Have the authorized operator run the scoped observer with that assignment, credential and trusted Backend origin. The upload grant expires after 15 minutes; do not widen scope or change the endpoint to bypass an error.
7.  Ask the operator to return the capture ID and retained result receipt after the observer finishes. An authorized workspace user can retrieve the receipt through `GET /v1/discovery/network-captures/{capture_id}`; the setup form does not open it automatically. Inspect scope, observed time and omission/attribution diagnostics. An issued grant or an empty result is not proof of a successful capture or an idle workload.

**Revoke this upload grant** is available while the once-shown grant panel is open. **Credential saved** clears that panel and its revoke button; retain the capture ID privately. For later revocation, an owner/admin uses the authorized `DELETE /v1/discovery/network-captures/{capture_id}` API or asks the workspace operator to do so. Revocation prevents further uploads. Stop the customer-side capture process through its operator procedure as well; it does not stop customer applications or remove sensors.

## 2\. Connect a continuous observer

1.  Under **Continuous network reporting**, choose **Connect continuous observer**.
2.  Select **Observer source**, enter the exact **Node scope** and **Service metadata namespaces**, then choose **Upload interval**, **Credential lifetime** and **Window retention**.
3.  Choose **Register observer**. Privately save **Observer upload credential**, use **Download observer assignment**, then select **Observer credential saved**.

4.  Have the operator install/configure the separately approved sensors and customer-run process using that exact assignment. Registration alone does not start them or change workload permissions.
5.  On **Discovery → Overview**, inspect **Where workloads connect** and choose the intended **Observer**. **Manage observer** returns to its registration.
6.  Read last contact, reporting/stale state, credential expiry and the expected reporting interval. Expand **Latest observer health** for each node’s sensor readiness, stream status, input events, omitted events and diagnostics.

7.  Confirm a newly completed window and its sequence/time after the process reports. Refresh and verify retained evidence. A Ready Pod or running process does not establish complete kernel capture.

## 3\. Stop reporting and retain the right evidence

Choose **Revoke observer reporting** for the intended registration when retiring it. New windows are rejected and a connected observer exits at its next request. Stop/remove customer-side processes and node sensors separately through the cluster operator. Existing customer workloads keep running; retained windows follow their retention policy.

## Failures and limits

-   **No eligible sources:** authorize and enable the customer Kubernetes source first. Setup lists the first 50 eligible candidates; do not substitute an unrelated source.
-   **No continuous observer report available / No recent activity window:** check real installation, credential validity, scope and reporting before concluding no activity occurred.
-   Service matching uses collected ClusterIP/port evidence. TCP observation does not identify application requests, infer tools or prove a successful business action.
-   The live view is bounded to 60 windows and 500 connection groups. Read truncation/omission notices and observed time; process restarts can leave gaps. Kernel loss can remain unknown.
-   Credential expiry, retention and last contact are different boundaries. An old retained capture does not establish current reporting health.

Continue with [runtime call metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/runtime-and-blast-radius.md), [inventory collection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/inventory.md) or [SDK call controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/call-gates.md).

---

# Inspect runtime activity and blast radius

> Connect a reporter to one workload version, inspect observed calls and compare them with collected access evidence.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/discovery/runtime-and-blast-radius/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · owner, admin · Walkthrough verification in progress. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

> **Walkthrough limits:** Source reviewed; live walkthrough and required screenshots pending.

Guide in progress

The local reporter setup is checked. Delivery to Discovery and the runtime and blast-radius views still need a complete walkthrough.

Follow application-reported model/tool activity for one deployment and compare it with collected potential access. Success means the intended binding receives real instrumented calls and you can trace each visible relationship to its evidence and time boundary.

## Before you start

An **Owner** or **Admin** enrolls reporting. Any signed-in tenant user can inspect accessible evidence. First [connect an authorized infrastructure source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/inventory.md) and collect the workload. Install the compatible Martian SDK in that customer application and explicitly instrument its normal model/tool calls. Do not report invented calls to make a diagram look complete.

Deployment, environment and version labels attribute reports; they do not attest the running binary. Use a separate binding for each intended environment/version and keep assessment traffic distinguishable from other traffic.

## Connect runtime reporting

1.  Open **Discovery → Sources → Runtime reporting**, then **Connect runtime reporter**.
2.  Use **Find workload**, choose **Discovered workload**, then enter **Deployment label**, **Environment** and **Deployed version**. The first 50 search matches are listed; narrow the search if necessary.
3.  Click **Create runtime binding**.

4.  Privately save the Binding ID and once-shown **Runtime credential**. Mount the credential as a read-only secret file in that workload and configure its SDK reporter with the trusted Backend HTTPS origin and binding. Click **Credential saved** to clear the credential panel.
5.  Start one reporter per customer application process, create a trace for each invocation and instrument the actual model/tool calls. A successful report is metadata about that call, not an assertion that a downstream business action happened.
6.  Run a bounded legitimate synthetic task through the real application. Check its reporter delivery counters/logs and retained binding after refresh. Missing dashboard events do not establish that no calls occurred: delivery can fail or be dropped.

## Integrate one real call

[Download report\_once.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/runtime-reporting/report_once.py) for a bounded integration using the SDK’s `martian_redteam.runtime.RuntimeReporter`. Install the [SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md) in the intended enrolled workload, alongside your application’s dependencies. This example is source reviewed and locally checked for imports/setup failure; real Discovery delivery remains unqualified.

Use a trusted module that exposes your existing real model/tool call as a sync or async function. The JSON input file supplies its keyword arguments. Do not put business requests at module import time. Run the helper only in the workload/version that the binding actually describes, using a legitimate authorized synthetic task.

```sh
export MARTIAN_API_URL='https://YOUR-APPROVED-BACKEND-ORIGIN'
export MARTIAN_RUNTIME_BINDING_ID='YOUR-BINDING-UUID'
export MARTIAN_RUNTIME_TOKEN_FILE='/absolute/private/runtime-credential'
.venv/bin/python report_once.py \
  --callback-file ./my_tools.py --callback-function lookup_order \
  --input-file ./private-test-input.json \
  --kind tool --system support --name lookup_order
```

Replace the file/function and trusted kind/system/name with your real integration. For `lookup_order(order_id=...)`, the private input file is a JSON object such as `{"order_id":"YOUR-AUTHORIZED-TEST-ORDER"}`. The runtime credential is distinct from the platform SDK key; the reporter does not load a `.env` file.

The helper starts one reporter, creates one trace and places the **actual callable** inside `trace.call(...)`. It marks success only after the function returns, waits a bounded interval for the reporter’s single delivery attempt, then closes. Its own summary contains trace ID and delivery counters rather than inputs, outputs or secrets; keep any logs written by your application private too. An async application should reuse one reporter per process instead of starting this helper for each production request. Configure timeouts in the real callback/client; the reporter does not cancel a blocked synchronous business request.

| Exit | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Callable completed and the metadata upload was acknowledged; inspect the corresponding retained event |
| 1 | The callable raised an error; inspect the private application evidence and delivery counters |
| 2 | Setup failed before the observed call |
| 3 | Callable completed, but metadata delivery was not confirmed |

Reporting is separate from business execution. **Do not repeat the callable merely because delivery failed or the dashboard is empty.** `close()` is not a flush/retry: pending or uncertain delivery can be lost and is reflected in `delivery_failed` / `dropped`. Compare the printed trace ID, exact binding, time and call target with retained Runtime activity after refresh; counters alone do not establish business effects.

This minimal integration emits call metadata. Resource links require explicit response-ID mapping through `RuntimeResourceRule` / `trace.resources(...)`; native Kubernetes request matching is a separate opt-in (`native_kubernetes=True` with actual request metadata). Neither is enabled or claimed by this helper. Ask the integrator for mappings supported by your real client contract before relying on those map layers.

## Inspect the runtime map

1.  Open **Discovery → Overview → Runtime activity**, or the record’s Runtime activity view.
2.  Select **Deployment / environment / version** and **Time window**: **Last hour**, **Last 24 hours** or **Last 7 days**.
3.  Read **Where calls went**. Select a model/tool to inspect its configured name, counts, outcomes and recent reports. Use **Previous connections** / **Next connections** when additional targets are available.

4.  For a resource link, inspect its service/type, opaque reference, reported action, outcome and time. These links require explicit response-ID mappings in the customer integration. Use **Previous resources** / **Next resources** to page the displayed links.
5.  Check the bounds: aggregate counts cover a displayed latest-500-event window and individual details the latest 50 events. A selected aggregate can have no corresponding row in that smaller recent-event window. Resource/action links page by 12 for displayed tools.
6.  Refresh with the same binding/window and confirm that the actual synthetic call remains in retained evidence.

## Compare configured reach

1.  Switch to **Blast radius** and retain the exact deployment binding. Read the collection receipt/time and freshness of its access evidence.
2.  Inspect runtime-reported domains, collected identity/permission paths and shared configured peers separately. Open the relevant resource or evidence row to see its source and matching limitations.
3.  Use record details such as **Configured access**, **Network evidence**, and **Hosting & identity** to answer their specific evidence questions. A network window or an RBAC policy is not a substitute for an independently verified business effect.

4.  If a card links an assessment to this deployment, inspect the operator approval, artifact-equivalence declaration and drift status. An operator-attested mapping does not independently prove the deployed binary equals the assessed artifact.
5.  Treat any quantified sandbox loss sample or time-window projection as its labeled conditional scenario. Diagram distance, group size and ring placement are not a risk score or effective-access proof.

## Failure, freshness and limits

-   **No runtime reporters connected** needs enrollment and actual instrumentation, not another inventory refresh.
-   **Revoke reporting** rejects future uploads while retaining history. It does not stop the application, block a call or revoke an independently enrolled call gate.
-   A reporter credential cannot authorize assessments or read console records. Source and gate credentials are separate.
-   Opaque resource references remain within their binding. Unmapped resources, errors and downstream effects can be unknown; do not merge them across deployments by name.
-   Customer-reported success, configured permissions and TCP observations do not independently establish effective access, complete capture or business impact.

Continue with [network observer setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/network-observation.md), [SDK call gates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/call-gates.md) or [assessment outcome verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/reproduction-and-limits.md).

---

# Create and launch an environment

> Save a supported business environment, prepare synthetic data, launch sandboxes and verify assessment readiness.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/environments/create-and-launch/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · member, admin, owner · Walkthrough partly verified. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

> **Walkthrough limits:** Own beta Gmail environment save/reopen, built-in sandbox readiness, real seeded Gmail login/refresh, expiry extension and stop were observed. Shared generation failed before QA. Generated/personal worlds, optional file inputs, other simulations and agent binding/business checks remain unverified.

Partly verified guide

The built-in Gmail sandbox lifecycle has been checked in one beta workspace. Generated/personal worlds, other simulations and agent business checks are still being verified.

Create an isolated copy of the systems needed by a red-team assessment. Success means the intended environment revision and data are saved, each required sandbox is **Ready**, and the approved agent can use its configured bindings.

## Before you start

Use a **Member**, **Admin** or **Owner** account. Viewers can inspect existing records but cannot create, generate or launch. Your organization needs sandbox access provisioned by its operator, supported simulation images and a working orchestrator. Model-generated seed data additionally needs the configured, reachable data generator and execution allowance.

Use synthetic or approved samples. Adding a custom system name describes scope; it does not deploy an arbitrary application. For an assessment without sandbox tools, choose [endpoint-only testing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/first-assessment.md) instead.

The observed beta walkthrough used **Documentation mail lab 2026-11-13**, with **Gmail** as its only system. It saved revision 1, launched a working sandbox with built-in fixtures, and verified Gmail sign-in, refresh, extension and stop. Shared data generation failed before QA. Generated and personal worlds, optional file inputs and agent bindings remain outside this result.

## Create the environment

1.  Open **Environments → Create environment**.
2.  Enter **Environment name** and optional **Workflow**. Describe the task, normal records and approval rules in plain language.
3.  Select the supported systems the agent uses. **Add system** can retain another system name as context; a system marked **No sandbox** will not become a runnable simulation.

![Saved Gmail environment reopened at revision 1 with its synthetic workflow.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-configuration.png)

The actual saved revision is reopened for inspection: Gmail is selected and the workflow uses synthetic contacts. The original save returned 201; this capture does not create a duplicate environment.

4.  If useful, expand **Schema & sample data**. Choose **Schema or API definition** for `.json`/`.sql`, or **Sample records** for `.json`/`.csv`. Scope an input to the whole environment or one selected system. The maximum is 1 MB per input and 20 inputs. Inspect parsing errors before continuing.
5.  Click **Save environment**. When entered from the assessment wizard, the button is **Save and use**. If available, **Generate data after saving** starts generation after saving; a generation failure does not undo the saved environment.
6.  Reopen the row and check its saved revision and selected systems. Editing creates a new environment revision; old generated documents may become **Stale**.

For the bounded example, enter a workflow such as “Triage synthetic support messages and draft replies using only docs-example.test contacts.” Leave **Generate data after saving** unchecked if you want to inspect generation separately. Saving alone does not launch a sandbox.

![Environment save controls with Generate data after saving unchecked.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-save-options.png)

Save environment and the separate Generate data after saving option. This reopened revision was inspected and cancelled without another save.

## Generate or reuse synthetic data

1.  Open the environment’s data summary to show **Environment data**.
2.  Inspect the shared world and per-system states. Existing generated records may already be suitable. Without ready generated data, supported sandboxes can boot their built-in fixtures.
3.  Choose **Generate data**, or **Regenerate data** for existing shared documents. **Generate my own data** creates your personal variant. **New world** creates a new linked story and regenerates its system projections.

![Environment data drawer showing failed World and Gmail generation.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-generation-failed.png)

One accepted generation attempt ended Failed before QA. No generated data is ready; built-in fixtures remain available. Only other environment names behind the drawer are hidden for privacy.

4.  Wait for the world and required system documents to show **Generated**. Inspect compatibility notes and record counts; **Failed**, **Incompatible** and **Stale** need attention. Generation uses the model and can take several minutes. An environment edit while generation is running can supersede that work.
5.  Verify the data choice shown for each system. Launch selects your ready personal document first, then the shared document, then built-in fixtures. The current UI uses this automatic selection; it has no seed-document dropdown.

Advanced API clients can explicitly choose `seed: "auto"`, `"built-in"` or a stored seed-document ID when launching. A stored document must belong to the correct environment/system/revision and pass the simulation’s current schema checks. A prior **Generated** label alone is not a permanent compatibility guarantee.

In the observed example, one **Generate data** request was accepted, then both **World** and **Gmail** became **Failed** with “the graph failed before QA.” The saved revision remained available. The later launch reported **built-in** as its seed source; no generated-world success is claimed. The generator can incur model usage before failing, so a failed status does not establish zero cost.

## Launch and verify readiness

1.  Return to **Environments** and click **Launch** on the intended revision. Each supported system gets its own sandbox. Unmapped/custom systems are reported as skipped. Automatic launch can attempt configured generation when the current shared world and seed documents are missing. Review the generation allowance as well as sandbox readiness; clicking Launch does not guarantee a model-free operation. An API client can explicitly request `seed: "built-in"`.
2.  Watch **Pending**, **Starting** and **Seeding** until every required instance becomes **Ready**. **Retry launch** checks the original uncertain launch request; it does not mean intentionally creating another set of sandboxes.

![Assessment Environment step showing Sandboxes ready for the synthetic Gmail environment.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/environment-sandbox-ready.png)

The selected environment reports Sandboxes ready with Gmail running. This is simulation readiness, separate from an agent binding or independently verified business outcome.

3.  Open a sandbox’s **Details** to inspect its Application, API or MCP endpoints. Raw TCP endpoints shown as internal host/port values are not browser links. Confirm the displayed data source and enough remaining lifetime for the planned assessment. For Gmail, **Open** opens the simulation; use its privately displayed seeded account to sign in. Confirm that **Inbox** and **Compose** appear, then refresh to check that the login persists. You do not need to send a message for this check.
4.  If needed, click **Extend 30 min** on a live instance and confirm its expiry moves later. Use **Stop sandbox** when finished. The observed stop returned **Terminating** first; after refresh, that specific instance no longer appeared in the normal instance list. An older **Expired** instance could remain. Do not treat the accepted stop request or an empty live strip as independent proof that every underlying resource has been deleted.
5.  Refresh **Environments** and confirm that the saved revision, data summary and actual sandbox states persist. Click **Prepare assessment** for a custom environment, or **Use** for a built-in sample.
6.  In the wizard’s **Environment** step, check **Sandboxes ready**. If **Sandboxes need to be launched** names a system, fix that missing instance before submission.

## Failures and recovery

| Visible state | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Generator is not configured or reachable | Ask your operator to restore the generator; saving an environment does not configure it. |
| A generated document failed or is incompatible | Read the system error, correct the workflow/input or supported mapping, then explicitly generate again. |
| Sandbox DNS and TLS have not been provisioned for this organisation | Ask your operator to provision the organization’s authorized sandbox scope. Repeated Launch clicks do not fix it. |
| Ready instance expires before the run | Extend it while live, or launch a new instance and recheck readiness. |
| Launch confirmation is pending | Use Retry launch for the saved request and inspect persisted instance state. |
| Environment cannot be deleted | Stop its running sandboxes first. Assessment history remains separate. |

Sandbox details can show seeded account credentials. Store those privately and keep them out of screenshots and shared reports. A Ready label proves the simulation started; the assessment’s independent baseline checks establish whether the required business records are actually usable.

The walkthrough’s first instance expired naturally. A separate lifecycle instance was deliberately launched once for the Gmail/extension/stop checks; an uncertain launch was not resubmitted to obtain a clean result. **Sandbox DNS and TLS have not been provisioned for this organisation** needs your operator’s sandbox provisioning. Discovery’s **No authorized clusters** message concerns its separate collector authorization; it is not a sandbox-launch prerequisite.

## Delete a custom environment

This management path is source reviewed; deletion was not part of the captured Gmail lifecycle.

1.  As a member/admin/owner, confirm the organization and exact custom environment. Sample environments cannot be deleted.
2.  Stop its live sandbox instances and wait until they are no longer live. A stop acknowledgement alone does not clear the deletion guard.
3.  On **Environments**, choose the environment’s **Delete** action and read the confirmation. Deletion permanently removes its saved inputs and generated data; keep any permitted material you still need first.
4.  Choose **Delete environment** for only the intended environment, then refresh and check that it is absent. Past assessments and findings remain. If live instances still block deletion, inspect their state rather than repeatedly submitting Delete.

Continue with [agent sandbox bindings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/sandbox-bindings.md) and [configure an assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/configure.md).

---

# Compare evaluation runs

> Pair records from two completed runs, inspect output changes, and compare compatible scoring jobs.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/compare/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · all customer roles read/export · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Compare a baseline with a candidate to see which recorded checks improved, regressed or stayed unchanged. The comparison uses dataset record identities and retained outputs; opening it does not call either target again.

## Before you start

Any customer role can compare authorized runs in the current beta console. You need two **Completed** runs in the selected project. Use the same immutable dataset version with unchanged inputs and expectations. A new publication with another dataset identity is not interchangeable merely because its display name is the same.

For a small example, run the [first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) dataset twice, within your authorized target-call budget. Identical results are a valid outcome. To measure a deliberate agent change, retain the tested revision in your own release process and the connection’s declared artifact information.

If you used the downloadable HTTP teaching adapter, its [optional comparison variant](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/http-agent/README.md) gives a reproducible change. Retain the baseline, restart only that adapter with `comparison_agent:answer` and the same bearer/tunnel, record the changed revision, and run the unchanged dataset once. It returns `ready`, `hello` and `4.`: two canonical passes and one deliberate punctuation failure. A declared revision records your assertion; it is not independent endpoint attestation.

## 1\. Choose the pair

1.  Open **Evals → Compare** and confirm the project.
2.  In **Baseline**, choose the earlier run you want to retain as the reference.
3.  In **Candidate**, choose the other completed run. The UI requires two different runs.
4.  Leave both scoring-job selectors at **Canonical exact match** for the initial comparison.
5.  Click **Compare runs**.

![Distinct baseline EV-1001 and changed candidate EV-1003 with canonical exact match selected.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-selection.png)

Choose the completed baseline and candidate from the same immutable dataset. This comparison selects canonical exact match on both sides.

## 2\. Read paired coverage and changes

Read the paired-record count and the baseline/candidate coverage before interpreting the summary. Records absent from one run, unfinished/error outcomes, and other incompatible records are **Not comparable**, not automatically failures or improvements.

For canonical exact match:

| Change | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Improved | The baseline failed and the candidate passed for the paired record. |
| Regressed | The baseline passed and the candidate failed. |
| Unchanged | The paired pass/fail outcome is the same. The answer text may still differ. |
| Not comparable | A valid paired outcome is unavailable or the run/dataset contract differs. |

Use **Search comparison**, **Comparison criterion** and **Comparison change** to narrow the table. Inspect the expected answer beside both outputs before concluding that a change is useful.

![Three paired teaching records with one regression and two unchanged exact-match outcomes.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-results.png)

READY and HELLO changed case or whitespace without changing their passing scores. The deliberate 4. response failed against 4, producing one regression with full three-record paired coverage.

In the recorded teaching example, all three records pair: **0 improved, 1 regressed, 2 unchanged**. The READY and HELLO text changed but their exact-match outcomes did not. The extra period in `4.` caused the regression; inspect the outputs before generalizing from that count.

## 3\. Compare supplementary assessment jobs

1.  Choose a finished **Baseline scoring job** and a finished **Candidate scoring job**. Select both; selecting only one is not a complete comparison.
2.  Use jobs with matching scorer definitions, instructions, thresholds and native judge versions. Applying the same historical suite version to each saved run is one way to keep definitions consistent.
3.  Click **Compare runs** again. The **Comparison criterion** returns to **Canonical exact match** after each comparison; explicitly select the supplementary criterion you want to inspect.
4.  Open **Baseline and candidate scorecards** when available to inspect both coverage and scores.

In the teaching example, applying **Response format checks v1** to both saved runs produces these results:

| Criterion | Recorded change | Suite gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contains_expected` | Three unchanged Boolean values. | Both runs pass. |
| `response_length` | Two increases and one unchanged length. With the suite’s **Lower** direction, the increases are **Regressed**. | Both mean lengths, about 3.67 and 4.67 characters, remain below the ceiling of 80. |

Select `response_length` and **regressed** to inspect the two increases. The retained surrounding spaces in `ready` count toward its length, even though the table visually compresses them. A passing suite gate does not mean every response metric was unchanged, and a preference for shorter answers is a policy choice.

![Matching suite v1 jobs, response\_length and two filtered regressions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-suite-numeric.png)

The same v1 definitions pair all three saved records. Selecting response\_length and regressed shows the two longer candidate outputs and deltas of 2 and 1.

![Baseline and candidate suite scorecards with full coverage and passing mean-length gates.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-suite-scorecards.png)

Both v1 scorecards have complete coverage and pass the mean-length ceiling of 80. Their different means do not erase the two record-level increases.

A different rubric or gate policy can change a score without changing the response. Choosing v2 on one side and v1 on the other shows **Comparison unavailable** with a definition/policy mismatch. Select the supplementary **Comparison criterion** and **not\_comparable** to see its affected rows. Canonical exact-match counts remain a separate view of the original results; they do not establish compatibility of the supplementary jobs.

![Different suite policies show Comparison unavailable and three supplementary Not Comparable records.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-incompatible-suite.png)

Baseline v2 and candidate v1 have different threshold policies. The response\_length view reports three Not Comparable records and unavailable deltas.

Text/category changes retain their type; they are not silently converted into a numerical improvement. Different immutable dataset identities also cannot form a paired comparison: the recorded three-record teaching dataset versus the two-record SDK dataset produced zero paired records and five **Not Comparable** rows.

## 4\. Follow evidence and retain the comparison

1.  Use the baseline or candidate trace action on a paired record to inspect its **Trace details**.
2.  Check the recorded input/output and available attributes, then close the inspector to return to the same comparison context.
3.  Use **Export comparison** to retain the currently filtered comparison. Clear **Search comparison** and choose **All changes** when you want all paired records. The filtered response-length example exports two regression rows, with both scoring-job identities and criterion values.
4.  Refresh, select the same run pair and scoring jobs, and compare again. Confirm the retained run identities and expected paired coverage.

![Candidate native trace opened from the punctuation regression and retaining output “4.”.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-compare-trace.png)

The candidate native trace retains “4.” for the same arithmetic input; the baseline trace retained “4”. Both contexts were inspected. Reported tokens remain Unavailable for this deterministic callback.

**Open candidate** returns to the candidate’s saved run detail. The [results guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md) explains exports and provenance for an individual run.

## Failures and limits

-   **No completed runs**: complete two supported target evaluations in this project first.
-   **Comparison unavailable**: read the reason. Different immutable dataset identities, changed inputs/expectations or different scoring definitions cannot be repaired by changing the table order.
-   A run truncated at its target-call budget may have only partial paired coverage. Check the coverage note before generalizing.
-   Missing model/prompt revision metadata stays missing. A comparison does not independently attest what code was deployed behind an endpoint.

Next, [inspect traces and sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md) or [define consistent scoring suites](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md).

---

# Create and publish datasets

> Import, edit, validate and version organization datasets, and make editable copies of Martian datasets.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/datasets/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · member+ edits; owner/admin publishes; viewer reads published · Verified 2026-11-14 · Isolated local QA; original JSONL/CSV/JSON editing and role boundaries in Martian Docs Lab; separate immutable-version and Martian-copy publication in Documentation Browser Execution QA; pinned source baseline. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Build a reviewed set of input/expected-output records, then publish an immutable version that your team can select in Evals. Draft edits do not change the version pinned by an earlier run.

## Before you start

Use the current beta Evals console; see the [source baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md#source-baseline). Your organization’s setup must be **Ready**. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can author drafts; **admins** and **owners** publish organization datasets. **Viewers** browse published datasets without editing them. See [permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md).

Use synthetic records for a tutorial. Confirm that you have permission to send their inputs to the chosen target before running them. Dataset creation and import do not call your target.

## 1\. Create the draft

1.  Open **Evals → Datasets** and confirm the organization and project in the toolbar.
2.  Click **New dataset**.
3.  Enter a **Name** and optional **Description**, then click **Create draft**.

Names cannot contain `/` or control characters. The `martian:` prefix is reserved for read-only Martian datasets. Choose an organization name such as **Support response checks**.

## 2\. Import or add records

Save this two-record example as `support-response-checks.jsonl`:

```jsonl
{"id":"answer-one","input":"Reply with only READY.","expected_output":"READY","status":"ACTIVE"}
{"id":"answer-two","input":"Reply with only HELLO.","expected_output":"HELLO","status":"ACTIVE"}
```

1.  Choose **Import file**, then use **File (up to 20 MiB)** in **Import records** to select the file.
2.  Confirm **2 new · 0 updated · 2 records after import**. Matching record IDs update existing draft records; other IDs add records.
3.  Click **Import** to apply the previewed file.

![JSONL import preview with two new records, zero updates and two records after import.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-import.png)

Confirm two new records and zero updates before Import. This preview matches the two-line JSONL example.

JSON and CSV are also supported; see [more editing and import options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md#more-editing-and-import-options) below.

## 3\. Check automatic validation

After importing this example, confirm **2 records**, **2 usable in runs** and **0 archived**. The draft editor automatically displays these counts, missing input/expected-output counts and a **Version** hash. There is no separate Validate button.

For a straightforward exact-match dataset, use nonempty input and expected-output strings. Review missing values before publishing. An entire invalid upload is rejected, so an import error does not mean that its valid-looking rows were partially applied.

A draft supports up to 100,000 records, while an individual evaluation selects at most 1,000 active records. Keep tutorial datasets small. See [limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/limits.md) before importing a large corpus.

Your version hash depends on the dataset name, description and records. It does not need to match the example screenshots.

## 4\. Publish and verify the version

1.  As an owner/admin, click **Publish**.
2.  Review **2 records**, **2 usable in runs** and the version hash.
3.  Enter a meaningful **Rationale** of 8–2,000 characters and confirm **Publish**.

![Publish dialog reviewing two usable records, a version hash and a filled synthetic publication rationale.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-publish-review.png)

Review the usable count and version, then enter a rationale before confirming Publish.

4.  Wait for **Published**. New evaluation admission for the organization pauses while publication finishes; earlier runs keep their original pinned version.
5.  Open the dataset from **Published datasets**, inspect its records, refresh, and confirm the same published version is available.

![Published Support response checks version with two usable records and their expected outputs.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-first-published.png)

Published confirms the first two-record version. Refresh retained READY, HELLO and the same version hash.

A publication hash identifies the reviewed content. It does not prove that a particular agent passed those records.

## 5\. Publish a revised version

1.  Open **Support response checks** from **Published datasets**, then choose **Edit**. This creates a separate draft populated with the two published records. A published draft itself is read-only.

2.  Choose **Add record** and enter the following values, leaving optional metadata empty:

    | Field | Value |
    | --- | --- |
    | Record ID | `answer-three` |
    | Input | `Return 2 + 2 as a number.` |
    | Expected output | `4` |
    | Status | **Active** |

3.  Confirm **Add record**. Check **3 records**, **3 usable in runs**, **0 archived** and a changed **Version**.


![A separate Support response checks revision draft with the added arithmetic record, three usable records and a new version hash.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-revised-draft.png)

Check the new draft before publishing: three usable records and a changed content version. The earlier published version is kept.

4.  Publish this draft with a rationale describing the added case, then wait for **Published**.
5.  Reopen **Support response checks** from **Published datasets** and refresh. It now contains all three records and the revised version.

![Published revised Support response checks version with three usable records, including the arithmetic case.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-revised-published.png)

The revised version is Published with three records after refresh. The original two-record native version remained unchanged.

The observed example changed from two-record version `01a5a93d8ca8` to three-record version `1fc87b52fa5e`. The original published draft and its two native records remained unchanged. The catalog opens the current version; there is no older-version selector on this screen.

The revised publication initially reached **Needs review** after a service timeout. One supported **Resume** of the same operation completed it; see [publication recovery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md#publication-recovery). The first submission alone was not treated as success.

## 6\. Copy a Martian dataset

1.  Open a `martian:` dataset from **Published datasets**. It offers **Copy to my datasets** instead of **Edit**.

Your workspace’s available Martian packs can differ. The examples use synthetic teaching records, not a security benchmark.

![Read-only martian:documentation-versioning-pack with three records and Copy to my datasets.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-martian-source.png)

This synthetic Martian pack is read-only. Copy to my datasets creates an editable organization draft; your available packs may differ.

2.  Choose **Copy to my datasets**. The editable organization draft opens with the reserved `martian:` prefix removed from its name. Check its copied records before making changes.

![Editable documentation-versioning-pack organization copy with three usable records and Publish controls.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-martian-copy.png)

Copy removes the reserved prefix and opens an editable three-record draft. Publication is still required.

3.  Review the automatic validation summary, choose **Publish**, enter a rationale and confirm. Wait for **Published**.
4.  Reopen your copy from **Published datasets** and refresh. Confirm its records and organization ownership. Reopening the original Martian dataset still shows the read-only source.
