![Published organization copy of the Martian teaching pack with three usable records and its own content version.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-copy-published.png)

The organization copy is Published and survives refresh. Its separate native identity preserves the original read-only Martian pack.

The observed **martian:documentation-versioning-pack** became the separately published **documentation-versioning-pack**, with three usable records. Its version differs from the source: a copy has its own identity. The original Martian dataset retained the same records and version. Copying alone does not publish a draft.

To save failed records from an existing run, follow [Turn failed results into regression cases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/regression-cases.md). That walkthrough verifies direct copying and the alternative file-import path, including their different record IDs and the export-wrapper conversion.

## More editing and import options

Edit, archive, delete, or import JSON and CSV

Choose **Add record** to enter **Record ID**, **Input**, **Expected output**, **Status** and optional metadata manually. Select a row’s **Edit** action and **Save record** to change an existing record. The record ID is fixed when editing. **Active** records can be used in runs; **Archived** records remain in the dataset but are excluded from execution.

This separate **Dataset editing practice** example starts with three records. A temporary record was added, edited and archived, leaving four records with three usable and one archived.

![Dataset editing practice with one archived temporary record and three usable records.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/dataset-record-archived.png)

Archiving preserves the temporary record in this draft while excluding it from execution: four records, three usable and one archived.

To remove the temporary record, select only its checkbox, choose **Delete selected (1)**, inspect **Delete 1 record?**, then confirm **Delete**. Earlier published versions are kept.

![Delete 1 record confirmation for only the temporary archived draft record.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/dataset-delete-confirmation.png)

Review the selected count before Delete. The actual deletion removed only the temporary draft record; the earlier published version was kept.

After deletion, the draft returned to three usable records. One new CSV record and one new JSON-array record were then imported. Each preview showed one new record and zero updates; refresh retained five usable records after both imports.

![JSON import preview showing one new record, zero updates and five final records.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/dataset-json-import-preview.png)

The second additional import previews one new JSON-array record. The native import and subsequent refresh retained five usable records.

JSON accepts a bare record array or an object containing `items`. CSV uses a header such as `id,input,expected_output,status`; optional metadata columns begin with `metadata.`. In JSON/JSONL, `metadata` must be an object. Use one expected-output spelling, `expected_output` or `expectedOutput`, per record.

## Failures and recovery

-   For a stale revision or “reload” error, refresh the draft and review intervening edits before retrying.
-   Duplicate IDs within one upload, unsupported fields or malformed files reject that upload. Correct the reported rows and preview again.
-   **Discard** removes unpublished draft work. Deleting draft records does not remove earlier published versions.

### Publication recovery

If publication becomes **Stalled** or **Needs review**, open **Datasets → Publish activity** as an owner/admin and find the original row in **Publish operations**. New runs remain paused until the operation finishes or is aborted.

![Publish activity showing an interrupted three-record revision beside the earlier published two-record version, with Resume and Abort actions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-dataset-version-publish-activity.png)

This initial interruption kept the earlier two-record version published. Resume later completed the same three-record operation without asserting that native creation was never submitted.

Choose **Resume**, enter a rationale and continue from the saved checkpoints. Leave the assertion that an interrupted creation was **never submitted** unchecked unless that has been independently proven. Ask your workspace administrator or support for help when native submission is uncertain.

Wait for Published

An accepted **Resume** queues recovery. Wait for **Published**, then reopen and refresh the dataset to verify its records. Keep the original operation while investigating an uncertain result; creating another publication does not resolve it.

The observed three-record revision completed through this path. **Abort** discards the unpublished version, keeps the current published version and makes its draft editable again; that abort path was not exercised for this example.

Next, [run the dataset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) or [organize evaluation projects](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/projects.md).

---

# Run your first evaluation

> Connect an approved HTTP agent, prepare a small published dataset, and inspect a retained evaluation result.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/first-run/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · owner/admin to prepare dataset; member+ to run; viewer can read · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Run three synthetic requests through an approved agent and compare its answers with explicit expected outputs. At the end, you will have a saved evaluation with a result for each selected record, an execution status, and inspectable evidence.

An evaluation measures the behavior described by its dataset and scoring rules. It does not establish that an agent is secure against every attack. Use a red teaming assessment for adversarial testing.

## Before you start

-   Use the current beta console with Evals setup **Ready**; see the [source baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md#source-baseline). Explicitly choose the **Default** project for this tutorial; a missing, unavailable or archived project is a separate problem from organization setup. See [evaluation projects](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/projects.md) if Default is unavailable.
-   Use **owner** or **admin** access to create and publish the example dataset yourself. A **member** can run an already published dataset; a **viewer** can inspect results.
-   [Register, validate and approve a stateless HTTP agent connection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md). Dataset Evals supports approved HTTP chat targets. MCP, browser and session-backed targets cannot run this tutorial.
-   If you need a complete teaching HTTP target, [run the callback adapter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/http-adapter.md). Its deterministic callback recognizes the three questions below; public HTTPS hosting is an explicit prerequisite for hosted console calls.
-   Choose an agent that you are authorized to call. Each eligible record sends one target request; your target provider may charge for it.

If Evals shows a setup warning, use **Refresh setup** after your administrator has resolved it. Refreshing cannot provision missing access by itself. If setup is Ready but the project is unavailable or archived, select **Default** in the project toolbar or ask an owner/admin about the available projects; repeatedly refreshing setup does not restore an archived project.

## 1\. Prepare a small published dataset

Open **Evals → Datasets**, confirm the organization, then open **Project** in the toolbar above the page title and explicitly select **Default**. Leave Default selected through publication and the first run. Published datasets are shared across evaluation projects in your organization; the selected project determines where the new run belongs.

To make the example self-contained, save the following as `first-evaluation.jsonl`. These are simple instruction-following checks. For an agent intentionally restricted to another task, replace them with three reviewed examples of its intended behavior and corresponding exact answers.

```jsonl
{"id":"ready","input":"Reply with exactly READY and nothing else.","expected_output":"READY","status":"ACTIVE"}
{"id":"hello","input":"Reply with exactly HELLO and nothing else.","expected_output":"HELLO","status":"ACTIVE"}
{"id":"four","input":"What is 2 + 2? Reply with only the digit 4.","expected_output":"4","status":"ACTIVE"}
```

1.  Click **New dataset**, enter **First evaluation** in **Name**, and choose **Create draft**.
2.  Choose **Import file**. In **Import records**, use **File (up to 20 MiB)** to select the file, check that the preview reports **3 new** records, then click **Import**.
3.  Check that the draft shows **3 usable in runs** and no missing input or expected output.
4.  Click **Publish**, explain the reviewed example in **Rationale**, and confirm **Publish**. Wait for **Published**.
5.  Open **First evaluation** from the published dataset list and inspect the records. The [dataset guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md) explains each authoring and publication control.

![Published three-record First evaluation dataset reopened after a full page refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-dataset.png)

The published dataset retains READY, HELLO and 4 with all three records usable after refresh. Choose Use in eval to configure a run.

## 2\. Configure the run

1.  Confirm **Default** is selected in the project toolbar. On the published dataset, click **Use in eval**. This opens **Runs** with **Run an evaluation** and the dataset selected. You can also open **Runs → Run eval**.
2.  In **Agent**, choose your approved HTTP agent.
3.  In **Dataset**, confirm **First evaluation**.
4.  Leave **Target-call budget** at **Up to 100 active records**. This is a ceiling: the three-record dataset contains only three eligible requests. Selecting 100 does not manufacture another 97 records.
5.  Click **Start evaluation** once.

![Run an evaluation dialog with approved teaching HTTP agent, published three-record dataset and 100-record ceiling.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-form.png)

The three-record dataset is selected. Up to 100 active records is a ceiling; this run has only three eligible target requests.

## 3\. Follow execution

The run receives an `EV-` code and opens its detail view. The progress indicator reports how many records have finished. Requests execute sequentially, with one active target evaluation allowed per organization across its projects.

![EV-1001 actually running with zero records finished and cooperative stop available.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-progress.png)

The admitted run is Running. Wait for recorded results; Stop after current request cooperatively stops further work.

Wait for **Completed**. If you need to stop, use **Stop after current request** and follow the [stopping guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/stopping-and-recovery.md). A completed run can contain failed checks or request errors; completion does not mean every answer passed.

## 4\. Inspect and verify the saved result

1.  Read **Results** and its **Input**, **Expected**, **Actual output**, **Exact match** and **Latency** columns.
2.  Click **Inspect** on a record. Compare the actual answer with the expected answer and inspect **View trace** when a trace is available.
3.  Open **Evaluation provenance** to inspect the recorded dataset and run identity.
4.  Refresh the page and reopen the same `EV-` run. Confirm the result rows and terminal state remain available.

![EV-1001 completed with three passed responses and retained results after a page refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-results.png)

The real teaching target returned READY, HELLO and 4. All three exact-match checks passed and the results survived refresh; this checks tutorial wiring, not production-agent quality.

Exact match ignores leading/trailing whitespace and letter case. Extra explanation or different punctuation can still fail. A failed check is useful evidence about this dataset; review the response before changing the expected answer.

## If something fails

-   **No runtime target** or unavailable agent: ask an owner/admin to complete connection validation and approval. Connection changes or revoked authorization require reapproval.
-   **An eval run is already in progress**: let the organization’s active run finish or stop it before launching another.
-   **Unknown dataset**, empty dataset or skipped records: reopen the published dataset and verify active records have usable input and expected output.
-   **Retry saved launch**: use that action to inspect the existing launch request after a lost acknowledgement. Do not create another run to work around uncertainty.

Next, [understand results and scores](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md), [compare two runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md), or [run evaluations from Python](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/evaluations.md).

---

# Collect human reviews

> Create typed review queues, answer required questions, verify completion and retain reviewer history.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/human-reviews/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · member+ reviews own/unassigned work; owner/admin assigns others · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Collect attributed human ratings on saved evaluation responses. A queue defines which results need which questions; it becomes complete only after the required answers and their native feedback are verified. Human ratings remain separate from the original automated scores.

## Before you start

Use a **Completed** run in a writable project in the current beta console. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can create queues and review work assigned to them. Owners/admins can assign or reassign another reviewer’s work. The reviewer must be an active non-viewer member of the same organization. Viewers can read authorized review results without submitting answers.

Choose a small set of synthetic results for the first queue. Each queue accepts up to 100 selected results and one to eight distinct required questions. Creating and answering human reviews makes no target or model call.

## 1\. Create the review queue

1.  Open the completed run’s **Results** tab and select the records you want reviewed.
2.  Click **Create review queue**; the action includes the selected-record count.
3.  Enter **Queue name**.
4.  Define the first required question using **Criterion**, **Question** and **Answer type**. Use Boolean, numeric, categorical or text; set the applicable numeric bounds or category labels.
5.  Use **Add required question** for another criterion, or select **Reusable question** and choose **Add saved question**. A saved question is appended; remove the unused default question with **Remove question 1** if you want only the saved rubric.
6.  Confirm **Assign reviewer**. Keep yourself or an unassigned workflow unless you have administrator authority to assign another person.
7.  Click **Create queue**.

![Real queue form defining required questions for one selected teaching response.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-reviews-queue.png)

Create a small queue and define distinct required criteria. Additional question fields continue below the visible part of this real form.

Choose criterion names that clearly distinguish the questions. A result cannot silently join overlapping review chains that reuse a criterion with a conflicting queue/question schema.

## 2\. Answer a required question

1.  Click **Inspect** on a selected result.
2.  In **Human review**, choose the required **Review question**. Read its instruction alongside the input, expected output and actual answer.
3.  Set **Review rating**. For Boolean questions, choose **Pass** or **Fail**. For other types, choose **Complete** and enter **Numeric answer**, select **Category**, or write **Text answer**.
4.  Explain the rating in **Review explanation**. A completed answer needs an explanation and a value valid for that question.
5.  Click **Save review** and wait for the saved state. Repeat for every required question on every selected result.

![Member text answer and explanation saved for the READY evaluation item.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-reviews-answer.png)

The member saved a text answer with an evidence-based explanation. This capture still shows MLflow pending for that answer; verify native persistence and queue completion in the next step.

Use **Pending review** when the answer is not complete. Saving pending work does not satisfy the queue’s required question. Finish or resolve pending edits before moving to another result when the drawer shows **Review changes pending**.

## 3\. Verify queue completion

1.  Open **Evals → Reviews**.
2.  Select the queue in **Review queues**.
3.  Inspect **Review queue summary** and the number of answers verified. Wait for **Complete**; a local save notification alone is not native-feedback completion.
4.  Use **Review filter** to inspect completed reviews, and open a review to read the explanation and retained history.
5.  Refresh and reopen the queue. Confirm its answers, reviewer attribution and completion remain available.

![Completed review queue with four verified typed answers after a full page refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-reviews-complete.png)

Complete means all four latest answers are verified: text, category READY, numeric 5 and Boolean Pass. These persisted answers are attributed to the synthetic member account.

For two results with three required questions, six latest answers must be complete and verified. A newer answer supersedes the prior answer in the current view while the history remains attributable.

## 4\. Reuse a stable question definition

1.  From Reviews, click **Manage questions**.
2.  Choose **New review question**, define the criterion/question/answer type and relevant bounds/options, and save the question version.
3.  When creating another queue, select that version using **Reusable question → Add saved question**.
4.  To change the definition later, choose **Create next version**. Existing queues retain their original question versions.

![Reusable Boolean review question at immutable version two.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-reviews-questions.png)

Create next version saved v2. The earlier queue retained the original v1 wording in both actual UI and API readback.

Question versions let reviewers use the same rubric consistently. They do not cause existing completed answers to be rewritten.

## Failures and recovery

-   For a stale review, reload the latest answer before editing; do not overwrite another reviewer’s work with an old revision.
-   If a save acknowledgement is delayed, wait and refresh the latest review before submitting another edit; another submission can create an additional history entry. Use **Retry saved review** after an unresolved acknowledgement. The same saved submission is inspected before another is admitted.
-   A non-admin cannot reassign work currently assigned to someone else. Ask an owner/admin to change the assignment.
-   If a saved answer shows **MLflow pending**, use **Sync saved feedback** to retry that retained assessment, then recheck the queue. Do not use **Save review** again merely to synchronize feedback.
-   A queue waiting for native feedback can show pending synchronization after local answers exist. **Reconcile native queue**, when offered, checks its recorded feedback. Preserve unresolved evidence for administrator review rather than marking it complete manually.
-   A rating is an attributed opinion under a rubric. It does not independently prove an exploit, permission boundary or business-side effect.

Next, [compare compatible scored runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) or [triage quality issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/quality-issues.md).

---

# Score saved outputs and define judges

> Apply code criteria or versioned model rubrics to completed outputs with explicit cost and provenance controls.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/judging/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · member+ applies; owner/admin defines native judges · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA (code + Boolean model rubrics). [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Add supplementary assessments to a completed evaluation without sending its prompts to the target again. Use code criteria for deterministic checks or a versioned model judge for an explicitly defined rubric. The original canonical exact-match results remain intact.

## Before you start

Use a **Completed** run in a writable project in the current beta console. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can apply scorers. Creating or versioning a custom judge requires **owner** or **admin** access.

Model judging additionally must be enabled in your organization’s environment and requires your explicit acknowledgement of provider charges. A disabled criterion labelled **Requires operator setup** cannot be enabled by acknowledging cost. Ask your administrator about availability. Reading or editing a judge definition does not itself invoke the model.

## 1\. Apply a code criterion

1.  Open **Evals → Runs** and select a completed run.
2.  Click **Score saved outputs**.
3.  Leave **Suite version** at **Ad hoc criteria**.
4.  Select the code criteria you need: **Exact match**, **Contains expected text**, **Valid JSON** or **Response length (characters)**.
5.  Click **Apply scorers** once and wait for the saved-output job to finish.

![Three saved-output code criteria selected, with model criteria unavailable.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-code.png)

Contains expected text, Valid JSON and Response length score retained answers. Model options require operator setup in this QA environment.

Only the saved outputs are scored. **Valid JSON** is a syntax check, not your business schema. **Contains expected text** is a substring check, not semantic correctness. Response length counts Unicode characters. Choose criteria that actually measure the property you care about.

Inspect a result’s **Assessments** after the job completes. The teaching response `READY` contains its expected text and has five characters, while failing JSON syntax. Its original exact-match result still passes. The recorded native persistence state tells you whether the additional feedback has been retained.

![Persisted native code feedback for the saved READY response.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-code-feedback.png)

READY contains the expected text and has five characters, but is not valid JSON. All three code feedback entries show MLflow persisted; the original exact-match result still passes.

## 2\. Add built-in model opinions

1.  Open **Score saved outputs** on the completed run and leave **Suite version** at **Ad hoc criteria**.
2.  Clear criteria you do not want, then select **Correctness judge** and **Safety judge** when they are available.
3.  Read and select **I acknowledge that model judging can incur provider charges.**
4.  Click **Apply scorers** once. Reopen **Score saved outputs** to follow the job, then wait for its terminal state.
5.  Select the corresponding **Assessment job** and inspect a result’s **Assessments**. Read the value, explanation and **Model opinion** persistence state together.

![Available correctness and safety judges selected with provider-cost acknowledgement.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-model-judges-selection.png)

The real local QA environment exposes both model judges. Only correctness and safety are selected, and the owner has acknowledged provider charges before admission.

The local teaching example produced six values across three saved responses, with zero judgment errors. Correctness and safety were both rated true for these benign examples. **Assessment identity** retained the model/judge revision; the original exact-match outcomes stayed unchanged. These ratings describe this small sample, not the target’s general security.

![Real correctness and safety model opinions with retained feedback and source identity.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-model-judges-feedback.png)

The saved READY result has true safety and correctness opinions, explanations and persisted MLflow feedback. Assessment identity records the Bedrock GLM-5 judge revision. One pending feedback delivery was reconciled without requesting another judgment.

If a saved value and explanation exist but their MLflow state is pending, use **Sync saved feedback** to reconcile that assessment’s delivery. Wait, refresh and reselect the original job. This does not request another model judgment. One assessment in the recorded example needed this action before all six native feedback records were retained.

## 3\. Define a custom model rubric

1.  As an owner/admin, open **Evals → Judges** and click **New judge**.
2.  Enter a stable **Judge name**, such as `answer_quality`, and a useful **Description**.
3.  Write **Instructions** describing what to judge from the saved input/output and expected value. For example:

```text
Assess whether {{ outputs }} answers {{ inputs }} with the required factual
content from {{ expectations }}. Return true only when the required answer is
present and the response does not contradict it. Explain the decision using
the saved text; do not assume external actions or unrecorded facts.
```

4.  Choose **Output type**: `boolean`, `numeric`, `categorical` or `text`. For numeric output, set **Minimum** and **Maximum**; for categorical output, enter one category per line in **Category options**.
5.  Click **Save version 1**. Reopen the judge and confirm the saved immutable version.

![Real Boolean custom-judge definition with a stable name and saved-text instructions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-definition.png)

Owner enters the docs\_answer\_present Boolean rubric before Save version 1. Saving the definition invokes no judging model.

A judge name begins with a lowercase letter and uses lowercase letters, digits or underscores. Keep the rubric specific and review it against examples before relying on its ratings. Saving a rubric does not establish judge accuracy.

## 4\. Apply a particular judge version

1.  Return to the completed run and open **Score saved outputs**.
2.  Under **Ad hoc criteria**, select the custom judge. Use the version selector beside it to choose the intended version, including a historical version if needed.
3.  If you choose **Policy compliance judge**, fill **Policy guidelines**.
4.  Read and select **I acknowledge that model judging can incur provider charges.**
5.  Click **Apply scorers** and wait for the job’s terminal state.
6.  Select that **Assessment job**, inspect a result’s **Assessments**, and check its typed value, rationale and persistence state. Refresh and verify the same job and feedback remain recorded.

### Create and apply v2

For the pictured differences, use the completed [comparison-variant run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) with the saved outputs `ready`, `hello` and `4.`. Your own responses can receive identical opinions when both rubrics accept them.

1.  Open **Evals → Judges**, find the same judge, and choose **Create next version**.
2.  Edit **Description** and **Instructions**. In this example, v2 requires the expected letter case and punctuation; v1 accepts the required answer despite those differences.
3.  Click **Save version 2**. Reopen the judge to read **Version history** and confirm that both definitions remain available. Saving v2 does not apply it to a run.

![Create version 2 preserves the judge name while allowing stricter instructions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-next-version.png)

The immutable judge name remains disabled. Owner prepares a stricter Boolean v2 rubric requiring expected case and punctuation, then saves it as a new version.

![Read-back version history retaining the stricter v2 and original v1 definitions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-version-history.png)

The real Version history panel retains both Boolean definitions, their original instructions and capture-time creation dates. Saving v2 did not replace v1.

4.  Return to the same completed run and open **Score saved outputs**. Under **Ad hoc criteria**, select the custom judge and choose **v2** in its adjacent version selector.
5.  Read and select **I acknowledge that model judging can incur provider charges.** Then click **Apply scorers** once.
6.  Wait for the new job to finish, select its **Assessment job**, and inspect the retained **Assessments**. Refresh and reselect that job to verify persistence.

![Two persisted opinions on the same punctuation response with different retained definition identities.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-feedback.png)

V2 rejects the extra period while the earlier v1 accepts the required answer. Both native feedback records, rationales, jobs and definition digests remain visible. The identical engine-v2 source suffix is separate from each rubric version.

The recorded v1 and v2 jobs produced three true and three false opinions on the same saved responses. Those ratings reflect different instructions. The target’s two canonical passes and one failure stayed unchanged; existing jobs retained their original rubric version.

### Use a historical version

The catalogue checkbox label names the latest version. Use the adjacent version selector to pin an older one; the historical v1 remains selectable after v2 exists.

To score another completed run with that older rubric, repeat the application steps at the start of this section, selecting **v1** before cost acknowledgement and **Apply scorers**. To inspect an existing v1 result, reselect its saved **Assessment job**.

![Latest catalogue label v2 with historical v1 selected for execution.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-judging-historical-version.png)

The checkbox label identifies the latest catalogue version; the adjacent selector pins v1. This actual selection was admitted against baseline EV-1001 after v2 existed and retained three native v1 assessments.

For a retained version record, select the relevant **Assessment job**, use **Results → Export JSON**, and inspect `assessments[].provenance["martian.native_scorer_version"]`. **Assessment identity** shows the job, definition digest and runtime source. A source suffix such as `martian-eval-judge-v2` is the judging engine’s revision; it is separate from your rubric’s version number.

## Interpret and recover

Boolean results can form pass rates; numeric, category and text outputs retain their own types. Coverage and errors matter alongside scores. A model opinion is separate from a verified security finding or independently observed business outcome.

Ad hoc judgments do not automatically define a passing gate. **Unconfigured** means no threshold policy was supplied, even if every Boolean rating is true. For built-in criteria, a [scoring suite](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md) can supply a threshold and minimum coverage. Registered custom rubrics cannot be attached to suite versions in the current console; their jobs have no suite-threshold control. Review their typed values and coverage directly.

A scoring request supports one to seven unique criteria. One active scoring job is allowed per organization. Completed runs are required. If submission is unresolved, use **Retry saved scoring request** to inspect that same operation. Stop controls are cooperative and may allow the in-flight judgment to finish; see [stopping and recovery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/stopping-and-recovery.md).

If feedback delivery remains uncertain, retain the run and job identifiers for administrator review rather than rerunning paid work. Applying a different job or rubric does not overwrite the first job’s provenance.

Next, [apply a reusable suite](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md) or [collect human reviews](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md).

---

# Read the Evals dashboard

> Interpret project trace volume, errors, latency, recorded usage and typed quality summaries without rerunning a target.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/overview/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · Any customer role · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA; native traces. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Use the project dashboard to understand the native traces retained for your selected scope. It summarizes recorded activity; it does not launch an evaluation or schedule model calls.

## Before you start

Any customer role can read authorized evidence. Choose a ready Evals project with retained native traces. This is **Evals → Overview**, distinct from an individual evaluation run’s Overview tab and from saved-score Monitoring.

The screenshots use the two retained requests from the [native conversation walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md#3-group-recorded-conversations). You can use any authorized traces in your selected project; opening this dashboard does not call the agent again.

## 1\. Choose the trace selection

1.  Open **Evals → Overview** and confirm the organization and **Project**.
2.  Use **Search trace content**, **Trace state** and **Trace order** to select the activity you need.
3.  Open **Filters** (accessible name **More filters**) for session, user, time, latency or assessment criteria.
4.  Choose **Apply filters**. Read the applied scope and incomplete-coverage notice before interpreting totals. **Refresh overview** rereads the selection.

![Real Evals project dashboard with two requests, zero errors, latency metrics and unavailable recorded usage.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-project-overview.png)

The two retained HTTP traces are included. The dashboard reports zero execution errors, P50 41 ms and P95 67 ms; usage remains unavailable.

## 2\. Read performance and usage

| Metric | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Requests | Matching recorded native traces, rather than a count of every provider call or evaluation case |
| Error rate | The share with recorded ERROR trace state; a failed quality check is a separate result |
| P50 / P95 latency | Percentiles of reported trace durations |
| Trace volume | Recorded activity over time; it is not a future execution schedule |
| Total tokens / Total cost (USD) | Reported usage in the matching traces, accompanied by reporting coverage |

1.  In **Recorded usage**, check how many traces reported tokens and cost.
2.  Treat missing reports as unavailable. No reported bill is not an independently established zero bill; partial coverage is not total provider spend.
3.  Check the selected time window and coverage again before comparing two selections.

![Recorded usage showing zero reporting coverage beside Boolean, numeric and categorical feedback summaries.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-overview-recorded-usage.png)

Neither trace reports tokens or cost. Three saved feedback definitions produce their own typed summaries; the separate expectation is excluded.

## 3\. Interpret Quality summary

1.  Read **Assessment**, **Type**, **Recorded values** and **Result** together.
2.  Boolean feedback can show pass rates. Numeric feedback can show means. Categorical/text values retain their recorded-value counts rather than becoming pass percentages.
3.  [Inspect the underlying traces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md) when a summary needs explanation. Use [native annotations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/trace-annotations.md) when you intend to add a human opinion or expectation.

For example, feedback named `response_correct` appears as **response correct**. A single Pass gives **100% pass** for that one recorded judgment; a numeric rating of `4.5` gives **Mean 4.5**. Text feedback appears as **Categorical**, with the text and its count. These examples describe the saved opinions, rather than independently verifying the response.

These are native feedback aggregates. They do not replace canonical exact-match results, a versioned suite gate or verified security outcomes. For gate history, choose **Monitoring** and follow [suites and monitoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md).

## Failures and limits

-   Aggregates inspect at most 1,000 matching traces. Narrow the selection when coverage is incomplete; do not describe a bounded sample as all history.
-   After a read error, use **Refresh overview** and retain the scope/error if it persists. Reading the dashboard does not repair missing instrumentation.
-   An empty selection can mean missing telemetry or restrictive filters. It does not establish that the application made no requests.

Continue with [trace inspection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md) or [individual run results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md).

---

# Organize evaluation projects

> Select, create and archive projects while preserving organization boundaries and historical evaluation evidence.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/projects/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · owner/admin creates/archives; all customer roles browse · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Use projects to group evaluation runs, traces, judge definitions and review work inside your organization. The project selector determines the context for the Evals page you are viewing. Published datasets are shared across the organization’s projects.

## Before you start

Use an organization with ready Evals setup in the current beta console. Any customer role can browse authorized projects. Creating or archiving a project requires **owner** or **admin** access. A project is an evaluation grouping, not another organization or a permission grant to a different tenant.

To verify run history in the new project, have an approved agent and a small published dataset ready. Complete the setup in [your first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) if these are missing.

## 1\. Select a project

1.  Open **Evals** and locate the organization/project toolbar above the page title.
2.  Check the organization name and your role.
3.  Open **Project** and choose **Default** or a named ready project.
4.  Move between **Runs**, **Traces** and other Evals sections. The selected project remains part of that navigation.

![Default project selected above the real retained run list.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-projects-selector.png)

The Project control selects the evaluation context. Default shows the earlier runs; the separate Teaching regressions project retained EV-1005.

Runs and trace views are project scoped. Datasets remain available across projects in the same organization. Selecting another project does not copy datasets or give you access to another organization.

## 2\. Create a project

1.  As an owner/admin, click **New project**.
2.  In **New evaluation project**, enter a **Name** and optional **Description** that describe the evaluation work.
3.  Click **Create project** once.
4.  Wait for the new project to appear selected in the toolbar. Open **Runs** to begin work in it.

![New evaluation project form with a synthetic name and description.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-projects-create.png)

Enter a name and description, then create the project once. This capture is the reviewed form before submission; the actual request created a ready project.

Creating a project establishes its evaluation context; it does not call an agent or run a model judge. If setup returns an unresolved response, use **Retry project setup** to inspect the saved setup request rather than creating an identically named replacement.

## 3\. Verify retained scope

1.  Refresh the page and confirm the named project is still selected.
2.  If the project is empty, click **Run eval** and follow [Configure the run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md#2-configure-the-run), keeping your new project selected instead of Default. Use the approved agent and small published dataset prepared above, then wait for the admitted run to finish.
3.  Open that run and confirm its run code and dataset identity.
4.  Change to **Default** and check that the project-specific run list changes.
5.  Return to the named project and confirm its saved work remains available.

An empty project list can reflect unavailable Evals setup, not an absence of permission to the whole console. Use **Refresh setup** after the underlying issue has been resolved. A URL naming an unavailable project is not sufficient to grant access.

## 4\. Archive a finished project

Archiving is an administrative terminal state in the current console: there is no restore interface. Use it only when the team is finished admitting new work to that project.

1.  Select a custom ready project. The Default context does not expose the same archive action.
2.  Wait for its active target evaluation or scoring work to finish.
3.  Choose the toolbar’s **Archive project** action.
4.  Read **Archive project?** and confirm **Archive project**.
5.  Verify the archived-project warning and refresh. Historical runs and traces remain readable, while new evaluation work is disabled for that project.

![Archived Teaching regressions project retains completed EV-1005 and disables Run eval.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-projects-archive.png)

After archiving and a full refresh, the historical run remains readable and Run eval is disabled. The example retains a changed-callback run with two passes and one failure; archiving does not rescore it. There is no restore interface.

## Failures and limits

-   A project whose state is not ready cannot admit new evaluation work.
-   Active target or scoring jobs can prevent archiving. Let them finish or use their documented cooperative stop controls before retrying.
-   Archiving does not delete historical evidence or revoke an agent connection. Manage connections through [Agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md).
-   Organization-wide concurrency still applies across projects: creating projects does not create extra target-run capacity.

Next, [run an evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) or [inspect traces and sessions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md).

---

# Investigate quality issues

> Find recorded execution errors and failed Boolean assessments, inspect their evidence, and retain attributed triage decisions.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/quality-issues/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · all customer roles browse; member+ triages · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Turn a recorded failure signal into an inspectable triage decision. Quality issues group execution errors and explicit failed Boolean assessments from the current trace selection. They help direct investigation; they are separate from verified red teaming findings.

## Before you start

Use the current beta console with retained Evals trace evidence in the selected project. Any customer role can inspect authorized issue groups. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can triage in a writable project.

To exercise a positive example, use a real saved run containing a failed Boolean criterion or recorded execution error. Do not edit a screenshot or fabricate an error to demonstrate a group. An empty issue view is a valid result when the selected evidence contains no supported failure signals.

For a free teaching example, apply the code criteria from [saved-output scoring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/judging.md#1-apply-a-code-criterion) to the first-run dataset. Plain `READY` and `HELLO` fail JSON syntax while passing exact match. This demonstrates a criterion mismatch to investigate; choose criteria that fit your real task’s requirements.

## 1\. Find the issue selection

1.  Open **Evals → Quality issues** and confirm the project.
2.  Use **Search trace content**, state/time filters and **Apply filters** to select the relevant requests.
3.  Read the coverage note. Choose an **Issue groups** entry to see its recorded examples and open count.
4.  If a group says it shows only some examples, narrow the search to inspect the relevant subset.

![Actual failed exact-match and JSON Boolean groups are found across eleven retained traces.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-issues-groups.png)

The candidate output is \[4.\] and the expected answer is \[4\]. The trace executed OK; its Boolean quality assessment failed. Numeric gate failures are not automatically Boolean issue groups.

Numeric, categorical and text feedback retains its type and evaluation policy. A low-looking number or a category named “poor” is not automatically converted into an explicit Boolean failure. The issue list does not establish all possible quality problems in the agent.

## 2\. Inspect evidence before changing status

1.  On a group’s row, choose **Inspect trace**.
2.  Inspect the saved input/output, execution state and relevant assessment or error in **Trace details**.
3.  Check the definition and recorded rationale where available. Determine whether this is a target error, a rubric disagreement, missing evidence or another concrete problem.
4.  Close the inspector to return to the same group and filters.

Keep the evidence distinct from your interpretation. An error trace does not by itself establish a successful attack or a production-side business effect.

## 3\. Record a triage decision

1.  Select the relevant trace checkboxes, up to 100 traces per triage request.
2.  Click **Triage N selected**.
3.  In **Status**, choose **open**, **investigating**, **resolved** or **dismissed**, as appropriate.
4.  Enter a clear **Rationale**: what you observed, your decision, and any follow-up or external fix reference.
5.  Click **Save triage**.

![Triage form selects investigating and records a concrete punctuation-regression rationale.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-issues-triage.png)

Record the observed difference and an appropriate status before saving. This form concerns retained teaching evidence, not a verified security finding or a deployment fix.

The decision records your signed-in identity, rationale and time with the selected traces. A triage status does not rerun the agent, change an expected output, repair a deployment or erase the underlying assessment.

## 4\. Verify the decision remains recorded

1.  Read the updated triage value in the group table.
2.  Refresh **Quality issues**, reapply the same filters if needed, and reopen the affected group.
3.  Confirm the selected traces retain the intended status.
4.  If a remediation changed the agent, execute a separately authorized new evaluation and [compare it with the baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md). Resolving a triage item is not evidence that the fix passed.

![The exact-match issue retains Investigating after a full refresh.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-issues-retained.png)

The refreshed selection retains Investigating for the same trace. Native readback also retained the account, rationale and timestamp; triage did not change the saved output.

## Failures and limits

-   **No quality issues in this search** means no recorded execution errors or explicit failed Boolean assessments were found in that bounded selection. It is not a security certificate or a guarantee about unexamined traces.
-   An unavailable/foreign trace cannot be triaged by guessing its ID. Confirm the organization and project.
-   Archived projects retain readable evidence while rejecting new triage work.
-   Aggregates inspect up to 1,000 matching traces. Narrow filters when coverage is incomplete; a visible group count and its displayed examples can have different bounds.
-   If the save fails, retain the intended selection/rationale, inspect the reported error and refresh the current evidence before retrying. Do not repeatedly submit different decisions to force a visible state.

Next, [retain a useful trace view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md) or [collect a human rubric review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md).

---

# Turn failed results into regression cases

> Copy a saved failure into an editable dataset draft, or import its exported records while preserving the correct expected answer.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/regression-cases/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · Member, admin or owner; observed Owner walkthrough · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA; Owner; saved-case authoring. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Save a failed record as a test case that can catch the same problem in a later evaluation. Finish with an editable draft containing the reviewed input, expected answer and source-run metadata. Creating the draft uses saved results; it does not repeat the target call.

## Before you start

Use a **Member**, **Admin** or **Owner** account in a ready Evals organization. The observed walkthrough used an Owner; viewers cannot author drafts. Start with a completed run containing a failed record, such as the [changed-answer comparison example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md).

This example uses **EV-1003**: expected `4`, actual `4.`. Keep the correct answer `4` as ground truth. Your run code and downloaded filename can differ. A separate publication paused new-run admission during this example; saved-result authoring remained available.

Choose one path per case. Direct copying and file export use different record IDs, so combining both in the same draft can add duplicate questions.

## Copy the selected result directly

1.  Open **Evals → Runs**, select the completed run and stay on **Results**. Read the canonical **Exact match** column separately from supplementary **Assessments**.
2.  Select the failed row’s checkbox. Confirm **1 result selected**. Select at most 100 records for one dataset action.

![One canonical failed EV-1003 record selected, expected 4 and actual 4.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-selection.png)

Select only the canonical failed row. One result is selected; saved-result authoring remains available while a separate publication pauses new runs.

3.  Click **Add selected to dataset (1)**. Under **Draft**, choose **New draft…** and enter **Regression cases from EV-1003**. Keep **Expected output → Keep the run’s expected output**.

![Add one saved result to a new draft while keeping the original expected output.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-dialog.png)

Choose New draft and Keep the run's expected output. The correct answer stays 4; the failing answer 4. is not accepted as ground truth.

4.  Click **Add to draft** once. After the success message, open **Datasets → Drafts** and select the new draft. The dataset page opens on published datasets by default.
5.  Check the input, expected output and usable count. Refresh and confirm the same record remains. The observed draft retained revision 2, one usable record and expected output `4`.

![Refreshed Regression cases from EV-1003 draft with one usable record and expected output 4.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-draft.png)

The direct-copy draft retained revision 2 and one usable record after refresh. Its source-run/result metadata was inspected without another save.

The **Edit** dialog exposes metadata linking the record to its source run/result. Cancel if you only wanted to inspect it. **Use the agent’s actual output** is appropriate only after a reviewer confirms that answer is correct; this walkthrough verified the original-expected-output path.

## Alternative: import an exported failure

Use a separate empty draft for this alternative.

1.  In the original run, select the failed row and click **Export selected failures (1)**. The downloaded `EV-1003-regression-cases.json` contains `source_run_id`, `dataset_id` and an `items` array.

The complete export is not an import-ready dataset. Importing it directly produces **JSON datasets accept only name, description and items**; the preview is rejected and **Import** stays disabled.

![Import preview rejecting the complete failure-export wrapper and disabling Import.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-wrapper-error.png)

The export's top-level provenance fields are not accepted by dataset import. This real rejected dry run changed no records.

2.  Save only the `items` array as a new JSON file, preserving each record’s values and metadata. For example, run this Python 3 command in the download folder, replacing the input filename if needed:

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path

export = json.loads(Path("EV-1003-regression-cases.json").read_text())
Path("selected-failure-import-ev1003.json").write_text(
    json.dumps(export["items"], indent=2) + "\n"
)
PY
```

3.  Open **Evals → Datasets → New dataset**. Name it **Imported failure from EV-1003**, then choose **Create draft**.
4.  Choose **Import file** and select the new JSON array. Review the preview: the observed empty draft showed **1 new · 0 updated · 1 records after import**.

![Corrected items-array import preview in a separate empty draft, showing one new record.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-array-preview.png)

The extracted items array previews one new record, zero updates and one final record. The draft behind the preview is still empty until Import.

5.  Click **Import** once. Refresh and confirm one usable record with expected output `4`. Its metadata retains the observed output `4.` and source identifiers.

![Refreshed Imported failure from EV-1003 draft with one usable record and expected output 4.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-regression-imported.png)

The separate file-import draft retained one usable record after one Import and refresh. Metadata preserves the source run/result and the observed answer, including its trailing period.

## Verify and continue

Both paths retained one usable record after refresh in their separate drafts. Neither changed the original run or published dataset. Review and [publish the draft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md#4-publish-and-verify-the-version) before using it in a new evaluation.

-   If creating a draft succeeds but adding the result fails, reuse that confirmed draft during recovery; another new draft can leave extra copies.
-   Import updates match IDs, rather than matching prompts. Inspect the new/updated counts before merging files into an existing draft.
-   A saved case does not establish that a later target has been fixed. [Run the published dataset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) to measure that.

---

# Understand results and scores

> Inspect record-level outputs, exact-match results, supplementary assessments, exports and evaluation provenance.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/results-and-scores/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · all customer roles read/export; member+ for supplementary mutations · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Read a saved evaluation from its overall execution state down to an individual input, answer and assessment. You will be able to distinguish a failed quality check from a failed request, retain exports, and explain which evidence supports a score.

## Before you start

Any customer role can inspect authorized saved runs in the current beta console. Complete a [first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) and confirm the correct project. Applying additional scoring or changing human reviews requires **member** access or higher; this guide’s read/export steps do not send new target requests.

## 1\. Open and filter a run

1.  Open **Evals → Runs** and select an `EV-` run code. Use **Search evaluation runs** and paging if necessary.
2.  Read the execution state and record counters. **Completed** means execution finished; it does not mean that every answer passed.
3.  On **Results**, use **Search results**, **Result status** or **Sort results** to find a record.
4.  Adjust **Rows** to page through results. Read **Input**, **Expected**, **Actual output**, **Exact match** and **Latency**.

![Completed evaluation result table showing three expected and actual answers, scores and latencies.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-first-run-results.png)

Completed is the execution state. Inspect each expected and actual answer and its score; this synthetic example has three passes.

| Record result | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Passed | The recorded response satisfied canonical exact match. |
| Failed | A response was recorded but did not match the expected answer. |
| Error | The request or processing path reported an error; read the saved error. |
| Skipped | The selected record was not executed or scored, for example after a cooperative stop or because it was unusable. |
| Pending | A result has not finished yet. |

Exact match compares the response and expected string after trimming outer whitespace and ignoring case. It does not ignore punctuation, remove an explanation, or establish semantic equivalence.

## 2\. Inspect a record

1.  Click **Inspect** on a result.
2.  In **Result and review**, compare the input, expected output and actual output.
3.  Read **Assessments** for any saved code-rule, model or human ratings. Each can retain its rationale, definition identity and persistence state.
4.  Use **View trace** for available execution evidence. **Previous result** and **Next result** let you inspect adjacent filtered results.

![Evaluation item inspector showing READY input, expected and actual output, latency and separate human review.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-results-inspector.png)

Inspect opens one retained record. Human review and supplementary assessments are separate from its original exact-match result.

Save or resolve an edited human review before navigating away when the drawer reports **Review changes pending**. Read [human reviews](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md) before assigning ratings.

## 3\. Interpret supplementary scores

For project-wide trace volume, latency, recorded usage and typed quality aggregates, use the separate [Evals dashboard guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/overview.md). The run-level Overview below describes this evaluation’s saved assessment jobs.

Open the run’s **Overview** and choose the relevant **Assessment job**. Supplementary criteria do not replace the original exact-match result:

-   **Contains expected text** checks a case-insensitive expected substring.
-   **Valid JSON** checks that the saved output parses as supported JSON; it does not check your application’s domain schema.
-   **Response length (characters)** reports Unicode character count.
-   Model judges and human ratings record opinions or rubric results with their own source and definition.

Boolean criteria can show pass rates and coverage. Numeric criteria retain numeric summaries; categorical and text values are not converted into a Boolean pass rate. A missing assessment is not a passing value. See [saved-output judging](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/judging.md) and [suites and quality gates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md).

![Original passing result alongside three separate persisted code assessments.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-code-feedback.png)

Supplementary code assessments do not replace canonical exact match. A JSON-syntax failure and a passing exact-match answer can both be correct under their different definitions.

## 4\. Inspect provenance and export

1.  Open **Evaluation provenance** and inspect the recorded run, dataset and available target/artifact identity.
2.  Return to **Results**, apply the filters you want to retain, and select **Export CSV** or **Export JSON**.
3.  Check the downloaded records against the visible selection. The result export follows the displayed filters; a small filtered export is not a complete-run export.
4.  Refresh and reopen the same run to confirm its results and assessment job remain available.

![Evaluation provenance with native FINISHED state, pinned dataset hash and unreported model and prompt versions.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-results-provenance.png)

Native FINISHED and three passed metrics were read back. The dataset hash matches publication; absent agent, model and prompt revisions remain Not reported.

Dataset versions and declared artifact revisions describe what was recorded at admission. Unreported model or prompt versions remain unavailable. An agent name is not proof of a specific deployed model or prompt revision.

## Failures and limits

-   **MLflow telemetry needs administrator review** means native evidence may be incomplete even when local results exist. Retain the run code and ask your administrator to investigate; do not rerun the target merely to repair telemetry.
-   **Sync saved feedback** retries delivery of an existing assessment. It does not justify inventing a missing value or treating an uncertain write as persisted.
-   Latency and token/cost data describe recorded values. Missing usage is not zero usage and is not an independently verified bill.
-   Quality scores, human opinions and model opinions are separate from verified adversarial findings.

Next, [compare runs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) or [inspect native traces](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md).

---

# Stop runs and recover uncertain work

> Stop target evaluations or saved-output scoring cooperatively, preserve retained evidence, and resolve uncertain submissions safely.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/stopping-and-recovery/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · member+ stops; all customer roles inspect retained work · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA (HTTP + code criteria). [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Request a bounded stop without discarding results that have already arrived, and distinguish an unresolved acknowledgement from a new launch. This guide covers customer controls in the current beta console; it does not require internal worker, database or MLflow administration.

## Before you start

**Members**, **admins** and **owners** can request stops for authorized work. A **viewer** can inspect status and retained evidence. A target run must still be queued or running; scoring must still have an active job.

Use a deliberately bounded, authorized example when learning the controls. A stop is cooperative: a target request or model judgment already admitted can finish and may incur its normal charge. Stop is not a way to revoke an already sent request or undo external side effects.

For optional practice with the [HTTP teaching adapter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/http-adapter.md), its [complete example README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/http-agent/README.md) includes `slow_agent:answer`. That genuine callback waits ten seconds. Confirm deadline headroom with your administrator before using it; the recorded local QA success used a 90-second request budget. Keep the original three-record dataset and stop after at least one record finishes.

## 1\. Stop a target evaluation

1.  Open **Evals → Runs** in the active run’s project.
2.  Locate its `EV-` progress row and finished-record count.
3.  Click **Stop after current request** once.
4.  Observe **Stopping after the current request**. Wait for the in-flight request and finalization to finish.

![Real stopping intent with one completed record and another response pending.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-request-positive.png)

EV-1007 shows Stopping after the current request after the first record passed. The next response is still pending; acknowledgement alone is not terminal completion.

A queued run may stop before sending any request. An active run retains the current response and skips the selected records that have not been started. Other projects share the same organization-wide target-run admission limit.

## 2\. Verify the cancelled result

1.  Open the run detail and wait for **Cancelled**.
2.  Inspect retained responses and **Skipped** rows. Do not count skipped records as passing checks.
3.  Open **Evaluation provenance** and inspect the native run state when available; a verified cancelled native run is recorded as **KILLED**. A queued stop can finish before a native run exists.
4.  Refresh and reopen the same run. Confirm its terminal state and retained rows remain available.

![Cancelled evaluation retaining two passing responses and one skipped record.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-cancelled.png)

After refresh, the same cancelled run retains READY/HELLO responses, two passes, zero errors and one unstarted skipped record. Two requests reached the actual teaching target.

In the recorded success, the stop was requested after the first record finished. The second in-flight response also arrived: **2 Passed, 0 Errors, 1 Skipped** remained after refresh. Native provenance showed **KILLED** with the same counts. Two actual requests reached the teaching target.

![Verified native KILLED provenance and matching two-pass, one-skipped metrics.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-native-killed.png)

Native provenance independently reads KILLED for this retained cancelled run, with two passed, zero failed, one skipped and zero errored metrics. The callback revision is explicitly customer-declared.

A cancellation acknowledgement is intent to stop, not proof that all physical work has ended. Wait for the terminal run state and relevant evidence before launching another evaluation. If the run has already finished, the UI/API can reject a late stop and keep its recorded result.

A cancelled run can also retain target errors. An earlier local attempt had two errors and one skipped record; its native state was still KILLED. Read the retained rows and any telemetry warning before interpreting cancellation as a successful target interaction.

## 3\. Stop saved-output scoring

1.  Open the completed target run and its **Score saved outputs** dialog. After **Apply scorers** admits a job, the dialog closes; reopen **Score saved outputs** while that job is still active.
2.  While a scoring job is active, click **Stop scoring after current judgment**.
3.  Observe **Stopping after the current judgment** and wait for the job to finish stopping.
4.  Inspect the selected **Assessment job** and the assessments already retained. Refresh and confirm the same job state and saved feedback.

![Real code-scoring job with Stopping after the current judgment and eight of twelve assessments scored.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-scoring.png)

The stop was acknowledged while eight of twelve code assessments had been produced. The configuration stays disabled while stopping. A separate local setup warning was visible behind the dialog; the retained source run remained Completed.

This stops supplementary scoring, not the target run that already completed. The in-flight judgment can finish; retained assessments are preserved, and unscored results remain missing. Partial coverage must not be interpreted as a passing full-run gate.

In the recorded code-only example, four criteria were selected for three saved responses. The stop was accepted at **8/12 scored**. The same cancelled job retained eight native assessments after refresh, with **2 of 3 evaluated** for each criterion and one missing value. The original target run still had three canonical passes. Here, “scored” counts assessments, including failing Boolean values; it does not count passing records.

![Cancelled scoring job retains two-thirds coverage while the source run keeps three canonical passes.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-stopping-scorecard.png)

After refresh and explicit selection of the cancelled job, each of four criteria shows two of three records evaluated and one missing value. All eight retained assessments had native IDs; the original target run still had three canonical passes.

## 4\. Resolve an uncertain acknowledgement

A network failure can occur after the service accepted a request but before the browser received its response. Use the action tied to the saved request:

| Screen | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Target-run launch | **Retry saved launch** |
| Saved-output scoring | **Retry saved scoring request** |
| Human answer | **Retry saved review** |
| Suite/queue mutation | **Retry saved request**, when offered |
| Project creation | **Retry project setup**, when offered |

Keep the original configuration while reconciling. These actions reuse the saved request identity to inspect/admit the same operation; they are not a request to run the target or paid model repeatedly until it passes. A request identity cannot be reused with different content.

## 5\. Handle setup, publication or telemetry failures

-   **Dataset updates are in progress**: new runs are paused while publication completes. Existing admitted runs may finish. An owner/admin can inspect **Datasets → Publish activity** for a stalled operation; use the [dataset recovery guidance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/datasets.md#failures-and-recovery).
-   **Refresh setup**: refreshes the readiness read after the underlying problem is resolved. It cannot authorize an unapproved connection or create missing model access.
-   Saved results with telemetry errors need administrator review. Retain the run/job code and error, rather than deleting evidence or rerunning the target to repair export.
-   A rotated, changed, expired or revoked agent connection can stop later target calls. Revalidate/approve through [Agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md) before admitting new work.

If uncertainty remains after refreshing and reconciling the saved request, give your administrator the run code, job identity, time and displayed error. Avoid including tokens, passwords or unneeded response content in support messages.

Next, [inspect retained results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md) or [start another bounded evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) once the organization is ready for new work.

---

# Use scoring suites and monitoring

> Save immutable scoring criteria and thresholds, apply an exact suite version, and inspect retained quality-gate history.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/suites-and-monitoring/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · member+ versions/applies suites; all customer roles read monitoring · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA (code criteria). [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Save criteria and quality thresholds as a reusable suite, apply a particular version to completed outputs, and monitor its retained jobs and gate outcomes. This keeps a quality policy consistent across runs instead of rebuilding it differently each time.

## Before you start

Use your organization in the current beta console. **Members**, **admins** and **owners** can create/version suites and apply them to completed runs. Any customer role can inspect authorized monitoring history. Have a completed evaluation in a writable project and understand the [meaning of its scores](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/results-and-scores.md).

Saving a suite makes no model calls. Applying code criteria uses saved outputs. Applying model criteria additionally needs enabled model judging and explicit cost acknowledgement. Custom registered judges are applied separately from these built-in-criterion suite definitions.

## 1\. Create a small code-scoring suite

1.  Open **Evals → Judges**, then choose **Scoring suites**.
2.  In **Suite definition**, choose **New suite** if another version is selected.
3.  Enter **Suite name**, for example **Response format checks**.
4.  Select **Contains expected text** and **Response length (characters)**.
5.  For `contains_expected`, set **Quality threshold** to `1`, **Better when** to **Higher**, and **Minimum coverage** to `1`.
