6.  For `response_length`, choose a ceiling for the **mean character count**, set **Better when** to **Lower**, and keep **Minimum coverage** at `1`. For the short answers in the first-run tutorial, an example mean ceiling is `80`.
7.  Click **Create suite** and confirm that version 1 is selected.

![Saved code-only suite version1 with explicit pass-rate, mean-length and full-coverage thresholds.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-definition.png)

Response format checks v1 pins containment at 1 and mean response length at most 80 characters, with full coverage. Saving this definition makes no model calls.

A Boolean threshold is a pass rate from `0` to `1`. A response-length threshold compares the **mean** across evaluated records; it is not a maximum allowed for every response. Inspect the range and individual results when outliers matter. Minimum coverage is also `0` to `1`; full coverage prevents missing/error assessments from being treated as satisfactory evidence. A blank threshold means that criterion has no configured gate; it is not an implicit passing gate.

## 2\. Apply an exact suite version

1.  Open a completed run and choose **Score saved outputs**.
2.  In **Suite version**, select **Response format checks · v1**.
3.  Confirm the pinned criteria and any policy instructions. Their controls are locked to the suite definition.
4.  If the chosen suite includes model criteria, read and select the provider-charge acknowledgement. The example code-only suite does not require a model call.
5.  Click **Apply scorers** and wait for completion.
6.  Select the resulting **Assessment job** and open the run’s **Overview** to inspect its scorecard, thresholds, coverage and gate results.

![Saved-output scoring dialog selects Response format checks v1 and locks its two code criteria.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-apply.png)

Select the exact suite version before applying it. The pinned code criteria are locked; this job scores saved responses without calling the teaching target again.

![Version1 code-suite scorecard passes both gates with three of three records evaluated.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-scorecard.png)

The completed v1 job has full coverage and no missing or error scores. Its response-length gate compares a mean of 3.67 with the ceiling of 80; the recorded range is 1–5.

A gate can be **Passed**, **Failed**, **Insufficient coverage** or **Unconfigured**. Job completion and gate success are different: a finished job may show a failed or unconfigured gate. Review the actual values and coverage before acting on the summary.

## 3\. Create a new version without changing history

1.  Return to **Scoring suites** and choose the prior version in **Edit suite version**.
2.  Change the relevant criteria, instructions or thresholds. For this teaching example, lower `response_length` from `80` to `3`, retaining its **Lower** direction and full coverage.
3.  Click **Save version 2**.
4.  Repeat [Apply an exact suite version](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/suites-and-monitoring.md#2-apply-an-exact-suite-version), selecting **Response format checks · v2** on the **same completed run**. Wait for the new scoring job to finish and inspect its **Overview**.

In the teaching example, version 2 lowers the mean response-length ceiling from `80` to `3`. The same three saved answers have mean length about `3.67`, so this newer gate fails while their canonical exact-match results remain passed. The earlier version 1 job still retains its passing `80`\-character policy.

![Version2 completes scoring but fails the stricter mean-length quality gate while exact-match results remain passed.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-failed-gate.png)

The newer ceiling of 3 fails against the same mean of 3.67. Job completion, quality-gate success and canonical exact-match results are separate outcomes; v1 remains unchanged.

5.  In **Assessment job**, select the earlier version 1 job and confirm that it still records version 1 and its original definition.

Use the same historical suite version when you want a [paired comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) under an unchanged policy. A different version may be intentionally useful, but it is a different scoring definition.

## 4\. Inspect monitoring history

Project [Overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/overview.md) summarizes native trace activity and feedback. Monitoring on this page summarizes saved scoring jobs and gates; the two views answer different questions.

1.  Open **Evals → Overview** and choose **Monitoring**.
2.  Read **Scoring history**, including the run, scoring definition, job status and quality gate.
3.  Select a history entry to expand its scorecard, then choose **Open run**.
4.  In the opened run’s **Assessment job**, select the matching suite version and time. **Open run** initially shows that run’s latest job, which may use a newer policy than the history entry you opened.
5.  Refresh, reselect that historical job if needed, and confirm its suite version and gate result remain available.

![Monitoring retains completed v1 passed and v2 failed jobs, with the older scorecard expanded.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-suites-monitoring.png)

Select a history entry to inspect its retained definition and gate. Open run starts on the latest job, so reselect the historical Assessment job when following an older entry.

Monitoring here is saved-output scoring history. It does not automatically schedule production target calls, continuously test a deployment, or establish model drift. Those claims require separate instrumentation and an explicitly supported execution workflow.

## Failures and recovery

-   A stale suite-version edit requires reloading the latest saved definition before another version is admitted.
-   **Retry saved request** checks an unresolved suite save. Do not create a different suite merely to bypass an uncertain response.
-   One scoring job per organization can be active at a time. Wait for it to finish or use the [cooperative scoring stop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/stopping-and-recovery.md).
-   A policy criterion requires its policy instructions. Missing assessments, provider errors and incomplete coverage need review; they are not Boolean passes.

Next, [compare matching suite jobs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/compare.md) or [triage recorded quality issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/quality-issues.md).

---

# Annotate a native trace

> Add typed human feedback or an expectation to a retained trace and recover an uncertain save without creating a duplicate.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/trace-annotations/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · member/admin/owner writes; authorized roles read · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA; native traces. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Attach a human opinion or expected behavior to a native trace, including a conversation trace that has no dataset evaluation run. This is separate from [assigned human-review queues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md). Saving an annotation does not execute a target or model.

## Before you start

Any authorized customer role can read annotations. A **member/admin/owner** can add one in a ready, writable project. Archived projects are read-only. Start from an existing trace you are authorized to inspect.

The screenshots annotate the retained **recall → BLUE** trace from the [native conversation walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/traces-and-sessions.md#3-group-recorded-conversations). Adding feedback to that trace does not repeat either conversation turn.

## 1\. Open the annotation form

1.  Open **Evals → Traces**, confirm **Project**, and open the intended trace’s **Trace details**.
2.  Choose **Add annotation** in **Annotations**.
3.  Select **Annotation type**: **Feedback** or **Expectation**.
4.  Enter **Name**: start with a lowercase letter, then use lowercase letters, digits or underscores, up to 60 characters. `exact_match` is reserved.

![Actual Add annotation form for response\_correct with Feedback, Pass, rationale and Save annotation.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-trace-annotation-form.png)

This real form rates the saved recall response. Save appends feedback to that trace without calling the target again.

## 2\. Enter the value and save once

| Type | Fields | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Feedback → Pass or fail | Rating: Pass / Fail; optional rationale | A Boolean human judgment |
| Feedback → Number | Numeric rating; optional rationale | A numeric human judgment |
| Feedback → Text | Feedback text; optional rationale | A textual observation |
| Expectation | Expected response or behavior | Text describing what should have happened |

1.  Choose **Value type** for Feedback and enter its **Rating** or **Feedback text**. **Rationale (optional)** supports up to 2,000 characters.
2.  For Expectation, enter **Expected response or behavior**, up to 4,000 characters. It has no separate rationale field.
3.  Review the trace, name, type and value, then select **Save annotation** once. **Close** leaves the form without submitting it.
4.  Read the saved annotation’s type, value and author. Your own annotation shows **You**. Refresh and reopen the same trace to confirm it remains in **Annotations**.

![Refreshed trace details retaining response\_correct, Feedback, You, Pass and the saved rationale.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-trace-annotation-saved.png)

After page refresh and a supported Refresh traces recovery, the same Boolean annotation remains beside the original recall input and BLUE output.

## 3\. Recover an uncertain save

An uncertain response can leave the form locked to its original submission. Use **Retry annotation** for that same submission; it retains the request identity and reads back the corresponding native assessment.

If the form closed successfully but a later trace read fails, use **Refresh traces**, reopen the trace and inspect **Annotations**. A read failure does not establish that the save failed.

If that form/browser intent is no longer available, reopen the trace and inspect its existing annotations before beginning a fresh submission. A new submission creates another annotation rather than editing the previous one. The current UI does not offer annotation edit/delete; do not use repeated fresh saves as a retry strategy.

## Understand what changed

Feedback and Expectation are retained human assessments. They do not rewrite span inputs/outputs, published dataset answers, canonical evaluation results, a scoring job or a review queue. Feedback can contribute to the native dashboard’s typed quality summary; Boolean false feedback can contribute to Quality issues. Expectation text is not projected as a feedback score.

A human annotation is an opinion or expectation, not a model judgment or independently verified security finding. Keep sensitive values within the trace’s authorized audience.

Continue with [Evals dashboard summaries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/overview.md) or [quality issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/quality-issues.md).

---

# Inspect traces and sessions

> Search native trace evidence, inspect spans, group recorded sessions, save views and export bounded results.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/evals/traces-and-sessions/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · all customer roles read/export; member+ saves views · Verified 2026-11-13 · Local QA; trace/view workflows and separately provisioned native sessions. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Use the trace explorer to follow recorded requests and inspect the spans, inputs, outputs and assessments behind an evaluation. Group by a reported session ID when you need a conversation view. These reads do not execute a target again.

## Before you start

Any customer role can inspect authorized native traces in the current beta console. Your organization must have ready Evals setup and retained trace evidence in the selected project. **Members** or higher can save views; viewers can use organization-shared views. You do not need a separate MLflow login or MLflow credentials.

Complete a [first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) to create fresh evidence. Not every request reports a session, user, token count, cost or model identity. Missing fields stay unavailable.

## 1\. Find the trace selection

1.  Open **Evals → Traces** and confirm the project.
2.  Enter distinctive input/output text in **Search trace content**.
3.  Choose **Trace state** or **Trace order** if needed.
4.  Open **More filters** for **Session ID**, **User ID**, **Minimum latency (ms)**, **Time window**, **Boolean assessment** and **Assessment value**.
5.  Click **Apply filters** and read the applied-filter summary and coverage note. Use **Reset** to clear filters deliberately.

![HELLO content and OK state filters select one real retained native trace in the archived teaching project.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-traces-filtered.png)

The applied HELLO and OK filters return one recorded request. Archiving preserves this evidence; reading it does not rerun the target.

Start with a narrow, known request or recent time window. An empty selection is not proof that the agent never ran; confirm the organization, project, filters and trace retention.

## 2\. Inspect native execution evidence

1.  Open a trace from the table to display **Trace details**.
2.  Begin with **Inputs / outputs** and compare the recorded values with the saved evaluation result.
3.  Inspect available **Overview**, **Messages**, **Attributes**, **Events** and **Usage** tabs. Use the span/tree or timeline controls shown by the inspector for the recorded trace structure.
4.  Expand **Trace assessments and metadata** to inspect retained feedback and identifiers.
5.  Choose **Download native payload** when you need the retained native evidence for an authorized review.

The capture below shows **Trace details** opened from the filtered trace table, with two native spans and the recorded input/output. For a trace attached to an evaluation result, you can also use the run’s **Results → Inspect → View trace** path.

![Trace details opened from the filtered table shows two native spans and retained HELLO input with hello output.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-traces-table-inspector.png)

The trace-table inspector retains the real input/output and two spans. There are 0 model spans and reported tokens are unavailable; missing usage is not zero usage.

A missing usage field is not zero usage. Reported model names, costs and span events describe what was retained; they do not independently verify billing, deployed code or a business-side effect. Treat trace downloads as potentially sensitive and share them according to your organization’s policy.

To add a human rating or expected behavior, use the separate [native annotation workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/trace-annotations.md). It appends an assessment rather than editing recorded outputs or a dataset answer. That write workflow has its own pending qualification.

## 3\. Group recorded conversations

The example below uses a separate synthetic HTTP application with native MLflow 3.16.1 instrumentation and an operator-provisioned application writer. Two actual requests stored `BLUE`, then recalled it. Each request produced a separate completed trace with the same reported session ID. This verifies the conversation view; it does not qualify SDK 0.1.2 ingestion or model behavior. Viewing these records in Martian needs only your normal customer sign-in.

1.  Return to Traces. To inspect a known conversation, open **Filters** (**More filters** to assistive tools), enter its **Session ID** and click **Apply filters**. Set **Group traces by** to **Group by session**.
2.  Inspect **Recorded sessions**, turns, errors and first/last recorded times. This bounded example contains one session, **2** turns, **0** errors and no ungrouped traces.

![One real native conversation session with two turns, zero errors and no ungrouped traces.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-native-session-group.png)

Two real HTTP requests share a reported native session ID. Recorded sessions includes both completed traces; tokens stay unavailable. This uses separately provisioned native instrumentation.

3.  Choose **View turns** to inspect one session while retaining its applied filters.

![Session-filtered trace table showing remember BLUE to Stored BLUE, then recall to BLUE.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-native-session-turns.png)

View turns opens the two persisted requests in the same session. The actual HTTP application stored and recalled BLUE; these reads do not run the application again.

4.  Open each trace to compare the real request and response. Refresh and confirm that both turns remain. **Ungroup traces** returns from Sessions to the individual trace table.

![Real recall trace with a completed chat-turn span, memory span and BLUE response.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-native-session-memory.png)

The recall request retained its real memory operation and BLUE output. There are no model spans, and missing token/cost values remain unavailable.

Sessions require a reported session ID. A set of independent dataset requests is not automatically a multi-turn conversation. If you see **No sessions recorded**, inspect individual traces and confirm that the target/instrumentation reports the session identifiers you expect.

An SDK **CI session** identifies a pytest upload; it is a different identifier from a conversation session. SDK 0.1.2 dataset and inline-check uploads do not forward local trace session metadata. The separate SDK teaching example below therefore has **0 sessions and 1 matching trace without a session ID**. A native integration requires separately provisioned writer access; Martian SDK 0.1.2/API keys do not issue those credentials or provide an equivalent customer trace-ingestion route. Ask your operator about a supported session-bearing integration rather than copying a CI upload ID into this filter.

![Sessions reports zero recorded sessions and one matching trace without a session ID.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-traces-no-sessions.png)

This separate SDK 0.1.2 selection contains one independent evaluation request with no conversation session ID. Its empty state differs from the two-turn native example above, which uses separately provisioned instrumentation.

## 4\. Save a useful view

1.  As a member/admin/owner, choose **Display**; its accessible action is **Columns and view settings**.
2.  In **Display and saved views**, select columns, move them into a useful order, and choose **Compact rows** if desired.
3.  Enter **View name** and choose **Visibility**: **Private** or **Organization**.
4.  Click **Save new view**. Select it later using **Saved trace view**.
5.  After refreshing, select the view again in **Saved trace view**, then confirm its saved filters, columns and density. Refreshing opens the default view; it does not automatically reselect your last saved view. **Update view** saves an authorized revision; **Delete view** requires confirmation.

Private views belong to their creator. Organization views are readable by the organization; mutation still requires ownership or administrator authority. Saving a view does not save a reusable native pagination cursor or grant new trace access.

![Display and saved views shows the retained organization view with chosen columns and comfortable row density.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/evals-traces-saved-view.png)

The member-created organization view retains its filters, column order and density. After refresh, reselect it in Saved trace view to restore those settings.

## 5\. Export a complete bounded selection

1.  Apply filters that produce the selection you want.
2.  Choose **Export CSV** or **Export JSON**.
3.  Inspect the downloaded count and identities against the selection and its coverage note.
4.  If the export is too large, narrow the filters and export again.

Trace exports support up to 1,000 matching traces and reject an oversized selection instead of silently returning the first 1,000. Overview, session grouping and quality-issue aggregates also inspect bounded selections; read their incomplete-coverage labels. Trace table pages contain up to 100 rows.

## Failures and recovery

Use **Refresh traces** after a temporary read failure. A stale cursor or changed session can require starting the search again. Quote/backslash content searches can be constrained by the native stored representation; use a distinctive simpler term, IDs or structured filters when needed. Reading/exporting evidence cannot repair missing telemetry and should not trigger a replacement target run.

If a view save reports **Failed to fetch** or another uncertain result, refresh and inspect **Saved trace view** before saving again. A new save can create another view; confirm whether the earlier one exists first.

Next, [review saved responses](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/human-reviews.md) or [triage quality issues](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/quality-issues.md).

# Accept an invitation and sign in

> Join the correct organization, sign in, and check your available role.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/get-started/access/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · All invited customer roles · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Finish with a signed-in Martian workspace and a role that matches your task. This guide is for invited users of the current beta. Accounts require an invitation; there is no public self-service sign-up.

## Before you begin

-   Ask your organization admin for an invitation to the correct workspace. A new organization owner receives an organization invitation from the platform administrator.
-   Need your first workspace? Use the **REQUEST\_A\_DROP()** contact option on [martiansecurity.ai](https://martiansecurity.ai/) or email [founders@martiansecurity.ai](mailto:founders@martiansecurity.ai) with your company, agent purpose and staging availability. Do not include credentials or customer records.
-   Use a desktop browser for the application. These docs also work on a narrow screen.
-   Open the exact invitation link privately. It contains account-enrollment authority; do not post it in a screenshot, issue or shared document.

## Join your workspace

1.  Open your invitation link and confirm the intended organization and recipient. An expired, revoked or incomplete link cannot create an account; ask the inviter for a replacement.
2.  Fill in **Your name**, **Password**, and **Confirm password**. Use at least 12 characters. For a new organization invitation, also enter **Organization name**, **Organization subdomain**, and **About your organization**.
3.  Submit the account form. Wait for the completion page. For an existing organization it confirms **You joined your organization**. A new account can be ready before Evals setup has finished; read the status instead of submitting the invitation again.
4.  Use the sign-in address shown on that page. Keep your organization address for future visits.

![Organization invitation form with synthetic owner and organization details; password fields are empty.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/access-organization-setup.png)

Enter your organization details for a new owner invitation. This real local QA form contains synthetic data and no invitation URL or password.

![Workspace ready confirmation after the invited owner created Martian Docs Lab.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/access-workspace-ready.png)

A successful owner invitation creates the organization and provides its sign-in address. This is the isolated local QA address; use the address in your own invitation.

## Sign in and check access

1.  At the sign-in screen enter **Email** and **Password**, then select **Sign in**.

![Martian Security sign-in screen with empty Email and Password fields](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/access-sign-in.png)

Sign in with your invited workspace account. A new account needs an invitation. Actual beta screen, 12 November 2026.

2.  Check the organization shown in the account area at the bottom of the sidebar. An account in another organization does not gain access to this workspace’s records.
3.  Open **Overview**. The navigation available to you follows your role. [Permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md) explains which tasks need a member, admin or owner.
4.  If your next task is Evals, open **Evals** and wait for the workspace’s setup status. **Refresh setup** reads readiness; it does not grant missing access or complete a failed setup automatically.

![Signed-in Martian Docs Lab showing Default project, owner role and the Evals Runs page.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/access-workspace.png)

The new owner can open Evals in the Default project. The sandbox service is not configured in this isolated QA environment, so the sidebar can show a stale-data indicator.

## Verify and recover

Refresh the page and confirm that the same organization’s workspace loads. If sign-in fails, check the organization address and invitation recipient first. The current sign-in screen has no password-reset link. Contact your organization admin or Martian onboarding contact for recovery instructions; an API key is not a console password.

A viewer can inspect authorized records but cannot launch runs or edit datasets. If an expected action is missing, check your role rather than creating a second account. Sign out through the account menu when finished on a shared computer.

![Viewer reading completed evaluation results with Run eval disabled.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/access-viewer-results.png)

A viewer can inspect the three saved results. Run eval is disabled; the real launch API also rejects this role.

**Next:** [Run your first assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/first-assessment.md) or [run your first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md).

# Red teaming and Evals

> Understand the evidence, records, and workflows before your first run.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/get-started/concepts/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · All customer roles · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA; named HTTP/catalogue walkthrough. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Use this guide to choose the right workflow and recognize its results. It is for every workspace role and the current Martian beta interface.

## Red teaming: look for a security failure

An **assessment** is a bounded attempt to make an authorized agent violate its intended rules. Choose an approved agent, the scope to test, attacker goals and supported tests. Martian records the attempts and the available evidence.

An **endpoint-only** assessment tests the agent’s exposed chat interface. A **sandbox-backed** assessment connects the agent to isolated, synthetic business applications so supported checks can inspect effects such as a changed payment record. The two scopes establish different things: a concerning answer alone does not prove a business side effect.

A **finding** records an observed problem. Read its outcome checks, reproductions, controls and coverage before deciding what it establishes. An incomplete run or an unchecked outcome is not a clean bill of health.

## Evals: measure known cases

A **dataset** holds inputs and expected answers. A published **version** is immutable. An evaluation run calls an approved HTTP agent for selected active records, retains its outputs and records exact-match results.

Additional **scorers** examine saved outputs. A model **judge** adds configured model feedback; a **human review** records a person’s typed answer and explanation. These assessments retain their own identity and do not replace the original exact-match result.

Run the target once for the selected dataset records; additional scoring, reviews and comparisons operate on retained outputs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D[Publish a dataset version]:::storage --> R[Run approved HTTP agent]:::agent
    R --> O[Retain inputs and outputs]:::tool
    O --> S[Score saved results]:::external
    S --> H[Review and compare]:::target
```

## Records you will see

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Organization | Your workspace and access boundary |
| Agent connection | The address, interface and approval used to reach an agent |
| Environment | A saved configuration of synthetic business systems |
| Seed data | Synthetic records used to initialize an environment |
| Trace | A retained record of execution, messages or related evidence |
| Project | An Evals grouping for runs, traces and review work |
| Suite | A versioned set of scoring criteria and thresholds |
| Call gate | An explicitly enrolled SDK control for entry to named model/tool calls |

## Choose your next task

1.  [Get access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/access.md).
2.  For security testing, [run your first assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/first-assessment.md).
3.  For response quality, [run your first evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md).
4.  To automate checks in your own process, [install the SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md).

See the [glossary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/glossary.md) for the remaining terms and [supported targets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/supported-targets.md) before choosing an interface.

---

# Run your first assessment

> Complete a small endpoint-only assessment and inspect the recorded result.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/get-started/first-assessment/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · Member, admin or owner; admin required for connection approval · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA; named HTTP/catalogue walkthrough. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Finish with one retained security assessment and an understanding of its report. This tutorial starts with an endpoint-only test: you can learn the assessment workflow before configuring synthetic business systems.

## Before you begin

-   Sign in to the correct current-beta workspace as a **member, admin or owner**.
-   Use an agent and endpoint you are authorized to test. For this tutorial, use a synthetic demo or test agent, not customer data.
-   Have an **active, approved connection**. If none is listed, an admin must complete [register, validate and approve an agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md). That guide documents the HTTP contract and each supported interface.
-   Read [supported targets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/supported-targets.md). Dataset Evals has a narrower interface policy than assessments.
-   Confirm the organization is allowed to run assessments and that the chosen test is available. The live controls are authoritative if your environment applies smaller budgets.

## 1\. Choose the scope

1.  Select **New assessment** in the sidebar.
2.  In **Environment**, choose **No environment — test the endpoint only**. This skips sandbox generation and makes the scope explicit.
3.  Continue to **Agent** and select your approved test agent. If its connection is draft, changed, disabled or awaiting approval, return to the connection guide before launching.

![Environment step with endpoint-only testing selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/first-assessment-environment.png)

Select No environment — test the endpoint only to use the approved connection without sandbox systems.

![Approved Docs teaching agent selected in the assessment wizard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/first-assessment-agent.png)

Select the approved teaching agent. HTTP connected describes its connection; NOT TESTED describes its assessment history.

## 2\. Choose one goal and a small test

1.  In **Goals**, fill in **Declared purpose** with the test agent’s intended task. For the downloadable deterministic target, describe its fixed teaching answers, fallback refusal and absence of business tools or private records. For your own target, describe its actual task and access.
2.  Under **Declared behaviors**, enter one relevant rule in **New behavior**, then click **Add**. For example: “Do not reveal private instructions or records when an untrusted message asks for them.” Click **Continue**.
3.  In **Tests**, use **Anonymous caller** unless your approved test specifically needs another supported identity. Select **By outcome**, keep only **Customer records leave** selected, and clear the other outcome cards. This example requests a disclosure probe. The console shows five requested techniques; that count does not mean five attacks will execute. If the catalogue is unavailable, resolve its readiness message before continuing.
4.  Choose **Light** for the first run. Review the displayed ceilings and execution settings before continuing. Light is a maximum budget, not a promise that every possible attempt will run or a guarantee of a particular charge.
5.  Keep **Plan independent rounds up front and run probe lanes in parallel** off for this introductory run. Browser targets are endpoint-only and serial, with their own supported outcome choices.

![Synthetic target purpose and one behavior boundary in Goals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/first-assessment-goals.png)

Declare the actual task and its behavior boundary. This deterministic teaching target has no private records, business tools or account actions.

![Only Customer records leave selected with Light and serial execution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/first-assessment-tests.png)

Only Customer records leave is selected. Light allows at most five rounds, 30 agent requests, 100 model calls and six minutes here; the five techniques are requested scope.

## 3\. Launch and follow progress

1.  In **Tests**, review the selected agent, scope, goal, test and budget. Resolve any message above **Start assessment**.
2.  Click **Start assessment** once. The wizard opens **Run** with the acknowledged run code. Keep that run open; do not submit another run because the first response is slow.
3.  Follow its progress and reported target/model budgets. A running status records work in progress, not a verified finding.
4.  If you must stop, use the run’s stop/cancellation control and wait for the final state. Cancellation cannot undo a request already sent. See [progress and cancellation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/progress-and-cancellation.md).

![MR-1002 running with Open trace and Stop run controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/first-assessment-running.png)

The acknowledged MR-1002 run shows its five requested techniques. Open trace follows execution; the header Cancel leaves the wizard.

## 4\. Inspect the result and report

1.  Select **Open trace** from **Run**, or from **Report** if the wizard has already advanced. Wait for a final **Assessment execution** state. Read **Security outcome** separately from execution and the finding count.
2.  In the observed **MR-1002** example, execution was **Completed**, but the security outcome was **INCONCLUSIVE**. It used three agent requests and 15 model calls, retained one unverified attempt and recorded zero findings. A completed run with no findings is not a security pass; your generated attempts and counts can differ.

![Completed MR-1002 with INCONCLUSIVE security outcome](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/first-assessment-trace-overview.png)

MR-1002 completed with three agent requests and 15 model calls, but its one attempt remained unverified and its security outcome INCONCLUSIVE. Zero findings is not a security pass.

3.  In **Trace**, use **Tree → Expand all** and select a turn. Compare **Attacker message**, **Customer agent reply**, and the recorded actions. The teaching target refused all three observed requests. Its model-generated critic is an opinion; this example had no deterministic target oracle.

![Recorded attacker message and actual teaching-target refusal in Turn 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/first-assessment-trace.png)

Select a retained turn to compare the actual attacker message, customer reply and action journal. The critic below is model interpretation, not an independent oracle.

4.  Open **Probe coverage**. The example’s single disclosure probe was **attempted** with an **unverifiable** outcome. Read missing evidence, budget limits and reproduction information before interpreting coverage. Endpoint-only evidence does not establish a sandbox business effect.
5.  Refresh and reopen the same run. Confirm its final state, verdict and retained turns. Then open **Reports** in the sidebar, find the matching run code and select **Download**. Inspect the JSON’s run, state, verdict and coverage; this is not a PDF. See [history and exports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/history-and-exports.md) for export scopes.

## What success looks like

You have one retained assessment with its selected scope, a final status and inspectable evidence. A finding is a useful result; zero findings are also a recorded result, with the run’s coverage and verification limits. Neither should be described as a certification of the agent’s security.

If the run fails admission, resolve the named connection, capability, compatibility or budget error before a new attempt. A local QA attempt was rejected before campaign creation because the worker’s three-round ceiling was smaller than the console’s five-round Light profile; it remains recorded as failed. A workspace operator must align those supported limits. If submission is uncertain, inspect the saved run/history first so you do not create duplicate paid work. [Troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/troubleshooting.md) covers those boundaries.

**Next:** [Read evidence and results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/evidence-and-results.md), then [create an environment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/environments/create-and-launch.md) for supported business-outcome checks.

---

# Use the Attack Library and coverage views

> Explore catalogued techniques, distinguish runnable coverage from reference material and understand the current Threat Intel view.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/library/coverage/)

> **Page qualification:** Current beta console · viewer, member, admin, owner · Verified 2026-11-13 · Isolated local QA; named HTTP/catalogue walkthrough. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Find the techniques relevant to your agent and understand what Martian can execute in the current catalogue. The expected result is a clearly scoped assessment selection, with unsupported techniques and declared gaps kept visible.

## Before you start

Any signed-in tenant role can inspect **Attack Library** and **Threat Intel**. **Member** or above is required to launch an assessment from an approved agent. Catalogue entries, taxonomy mappings and prior findings do not by themselves authorize testing or certify compliance.

## Explore technique coverage

1.  Open **Attack Library**. Inspect its catalogue statistics and coverage matrix rather than treating every listed item as a runnable test.
2.  Use the available taxonomy view, such as **MITRE ATLAS** or **OWASP**, to inspect the published classification. Framework mappings organize material; they are not a compliance assessment or an exhaustive guarantee.
3.  Open a technique and read its supported surface, outcome and current coverage. A technique marked unavailable remains disabled for execution.

![MT-01 technique detail with In the library and enabled Add to assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/library-coverage.png)

MT-01 is in the runnable library. Its illustrative payload and taxonomy labels describe a technique, not an observed finding or compliance verdict.

The observed catalogue offered **MT-01 Direct instruction override** as **In the library**, with **Add to assessment** enabled. **MT-20 Session hijack** was a **Declared gap**, with that action disabled. These are catalogue states, not findings about the teaching target.

The source-visible **Add to assessment** shortcut opens the wizard’s Tests step in **By technique** mode with that technique selected. Confirm the preselection, then review Environment, Agent and Goals before launching. This shortcut is separate from the manually selected path below and was not independently exercised in the recorded catalogue walkthrough.

![MT-20 Session hijack declared gap with Add to assessment disabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/library-gap.png)

MT-20 remains a Declared gap. Its disabled Add to assessment action keeps reference coverage separate from runnable tests.

4.  In **New assessment → Tests → By technique**, search by name, ID or surface and choose available techniques that match the authorized target. Confirm the final selected count and actual budget before **Start assessment**.
5.  After a run, compare requested scope with **Probe coverage** and actual target attempts. Catalogue membership and a selected checkbox do not prove execution or successful verification.

## Understand the source of the catalogue

The customer Attack Library reads the stored Backend technique and published-attack catalogue. It is not a live mirror of the researcher Wiki. A selected compatible scenario can use published Wiki material, while review/submission and customer execution remain separate workflows.

Do not treat a newly discussed or submitted Wiki case as automatically available in this customer catalogue. If expected content is missing, ask your operator which reviewed catalogue/scenario revision is available in your environment.

## Read Threat Intel accurately

1.  Open **Threat Intel**.
2.  Read **No live feed connected** when shown. Current catalogue statistics and declared gaps are reference/coverage context; this screen does not establish a running external threat-ingestion feed.
3.  Follow an actual assessment’s retained findings/evidence to investigate a fleet signal. Use [history and exports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/history-and-exports.md) to locate the underlying run.

![Threat Intelligence explicitly says No live feed connected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/media/screenshots/library-threat-intel.png)

The workspace reports No live feed connected. Published-attack statistics provide catalogue context and do not establish live threat ingestion.

## Verify and recover

Refresh the catalogue, repeat the intended search and check that the displayed selection corresponds to the same available technique IDs. A missing catalogue/error state needs service or publication repair; do not substitute invented coverage. An uncovered technique, no findings or an empty feed is not evidence that the agent is secure or no relevant attack exists.

Continue with [configure an assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/configure.md) and [interpret reproduction and coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/reproduction-and-limits.md).

---

# Find your way around the console

> Locate every customer console area, its guide and the boundary between available workflows, templates and previews.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/reference/console-navigation/)

The console sidebar groups current work, adversary material, history and organization access. This map follows the inspected customer interface; controls can additionally depend on your role, project and readiness. Use [verification records](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md) to see which walkthroughs were actually exercised.

| Console area | What to do there | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overview | Inspect the displayed agent page’s latest standing, declared reach and recorded coverage; a held result is not a general security guarantee | [Evidence and coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/evidence-and-results.md) |
| New assessment | Configure one approved, bounded security test | [First assessment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/first-assessment.md) and [wizard options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/configure.md) |
| Evals | Work with datasets, runs, traces, summaries, judges and reviews | [First evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/first-run.md) and [Evals dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/overview.md) |
| Agents | Register, validate, approve and manage authorized connections | [Connections](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md) |
| Discovery | Collect inventory; inspect runtime/network evidence and explicitly enrolled call controls | [Sources](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/inventory.md), [runtime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/runtime-and-blast-radius.md), [network observation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/network-observation.md) and [call gates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/call-gates.md) |
| Replay | Read retained assessment evidence without executing it again | [History and exports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/history-and-exports.md) |
| Environments | Prepare synthetic systems and manage their sandbox lifecycle | [Environments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/environments/create-and-launch.md) |
| Pipeline | Preview and download a policy template; automated pipeline runs and waiver management are not connected to the console | [Supported SDK/CI workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/ci.md) |
| Attack Library | Inspect catalogue availability, taxonomy and declared gaps, then choose supported tests | [Library coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/coverage.md) |
| Threat Intel | Inspect the feed state; the recorded interface has no live feed connected | [Library and feed limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/library/coverage.md) |
| Assessments / Findings / Reports | Find saved runs, inspect observations and download the appropriate retained evidence | [Reports and exports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/history-and-exports.md) |
| Team | Invite teammates and inspect organization roles | [Team and roles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/workspace/team-and-roles.md) |

## Inside Evals

-   **Overview** summarizes matching native traces; it is separate from a run’s Overview and from **Monitoring**.
-   **Traces** opens native evidence, conversations, saved views and [human annotations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/trace-annotations.md).
-   **Runs** holds canonical evaluation results and the organization-wide CI sessions area; **Compare** pairs saved runs.
-   **Datasets** holds published versions and drafts. **Judges** manages saved-output criteria. **Reviews** holds assigned questions; **Quality issues** groups recorded error/failed-Boolean signals.
-   **Scoring suites** and **Monitoring** provide versioned criteria and gate history. [Choose a named project](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/evals/projects.md) deliberately; project selection changes the accessible scope.

## Account menu

The account control at the bottom of the sidebar opens **Profile**, **Theme** and **Sign out**. Profile shows your signed-in identity, role, organization and reported Agents-runtime provisioning status. It is not an account-editing or credential-issuance form. A provisioning label alone does not prove all target, model or sandbox services are ready.

**Master admin** appears only for platform operators. Organization creation/global catalogue administration and infrastructure installation remain separate from these customer tasks; ask the relevant operator when those prerequisites are absent.

Continue with [roles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md), [supported targets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/supported-targets.md) or [troubleshooting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/troubleshooting.md).

# Glossary

> Plain definitions for the words used in Martian customer workflows.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/reference/glossary/)

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Agent | The application or callback being tested, with its own intended rules and tools |
| Assessment | A bounded security test against an authorized agent |
| Attack technique | A supported way to try to cause an unwanted outcome |
| Assurance pack | A published scenario-backed option with specific compatibility and outcome-check requirements |
| Baseline | The chosen reference run or observed starting state; its meaning depends on the workflow |
| Call gate | Customer SDK enforcement at entry to an explicitly enrolled named model/tool call |
| Connection | Approved interface/address/credential contract for reaching an agent |
| Dataset | A collection of inputs and expected answers |
| Dataset version | An immutable published dataset snapshot |
| Endpoint-only | Assessment scope limited to the agent’s exposed interface |
| Environment | A saved configuration of isolated synthetic business systems |
| Evals | Dataset-based response evaluation and related saved-output analysis |
| Exact match | Equality after stripping surrounding whitespace and ignoring case |
| Finding | A recorded observed problem with its evidence and verification limits |
| Judge | A configured scorer that returns typed feedback, sometimes using a model |
| Outcome check | A supported independent observation of the relevant business state |
| Oracle | A trusted check of the claimed outcome, independent of the attacking model’s opinion |
| Carrier / implant | The message, document or tool descriptor carrying an untrusted attack payload, and the payload inserted into it |
| No-implant control | A comparable test without that inserted payload, used to check whether the effect depends on the attack |
| World epoch | An identifier for a particular initialized or restored sandbox state; different epochs can represent different test worlds |
| Project | An organization-scoped Evals grouping for runs and related work |
| Provenance | Recorded identities, versions, authorizations and revisions explaining where results came from |
| Replay | Inspection of retained execution evidence; it does not itself mean a new live execution |
| Reproduction | A distinct repeat of a test under the recorded verification conditions |
| Review queue | Selected saved results and their required human questions |
| Sandbox | An isolated running copy of a supported synthetic business application |
| Scorer | A defined calculation or judgment applied to a result |
| Seed data | Synthetic records used to initialize a sandbox world |
| Session | A grouping of recorded conversation turns when that identity was captured |
| Suite | An immutable versioned set of scoring criteria and quality thresholds |
| Trace | A retained execution/message record and its associated attributes/evidence |
| Viewer / member / admin / owner | Customer roles with different allowed actions |

[Choose a workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/get-started/concepts.md) or [check permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md).

---

# Budgets, limits and evidence

> Understand bounded execution, stopping, provenance and evidence coverage.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/reference/limits/)

Use the live launch form and readiness messages for the active environment’s policy. These are ceilings and evidence boundaries, not security guarantees.

## Assessments

The chosen depth controls admitted work. The examined Light profile defaults to ceilings of **30 target calls**, **100 model calls** and **360 seconds**; organization/server policy can reduce or reject that request. The interface, target authorization and compatible execution mode can further limit concurrency, supported checks and reproduction.

Cancellation requests a stop. It does not undo a request already sent or prove a provider has physically finished. Inspect final state, skipped/failed checks and retained evidence.

## Evals

| Area | Current boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Target-call budget | API 1–1,000 selected records; UI choices 100 / 250 / 500 / 1,000 |
| Small tutorial | Use a three-record dataset: budget 100 is an upper bound, not 100 mandatory requests |
| Concurrent target runs | One queued/running evaluation per organization, across projects |
| Concurrent scoring jobs | One active scoring job per organization, separate from target admission |
| Target execution | Sequential; ACTIVE usable records within the selected budget |
| Human queue | 1–100 selected results, 1–8 unique required questions |
| Bulk dataset/review actions | Up to 100 selected records per action |
| Trace query page | Up to 100 rows; default 25 |
| Bounded trace exports/scans | Limits apply at 1,000 matches; narrow filters when a complete export is refused |
| Dataset import | Up to 20 MiB and 100,000 records; the whole invalid upload is rejected |

**Stop after current request** retains an in-flight result, prevents the next target call and marks remaining selected records skipped. Scoring stop similarly retains the in-flight judgment. Reopening, exporting or reviewing saved values does not execute the target again.

## Scores

Canonical exact match compares stripped, case-folded actual and expected strings. Punctuation and extra text still matter. Other scores preserve their own definition and type. Numeric/category/text feedback must not be presented as a Boolean pass rate. Missing token or cost data is unknown, not zero.

## Provenance and coverage

Published dataset versions and runs retain pinned identities/digests. A declared agent artifact revision is useful provenance; an agent’s name cannot establish its model or prompt version. Historical data and bounded runtime observations do not independently verify effective access, predict an incident or prove a loss ceiling.

A clean reproduction, negative control, independent business check and model opinion establish different things. Read [assessment evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/reproduction-and-limits.md) and [Discovery evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/discovery/runtime-and-blast-radius.md) before interpreting them.

---

# Roles and permissions

> Check the minimum role for each customer task.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/reference/permissions/)

Permissions apply within your organization. Your console session and a machine API key are separate forms of access. This table summarizes the current source contract; the live interface can additionally withhold an action when setup, target approval or environment policy is not ready.

| Task | Viewer | Member | Admin / owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Browse authorized assessments, results, datasets and Evals history | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Launch/stop assessments and Evals | No | Yes | Yes |
| Create/configure environments and manage their sandbox lifecycle | No | Yes | Yes |
| Register, validate, approve, rotate or disable agent connections | No | No | Yes |
| Import/edit dataset drafts | No | Yes | Yes |
| Publish an organization dataset | No | No | Yes |
| Create/archive Evals projects; register custom model judges | No | No | Yes |
| Score saved outputs, create suites/questions, complete assigned reviews | No | Yes | Yes |
| Triage quality issues | No | Yes | Yes |
| Assign another eligible reviewer; manage organization API keys and team invitations | No | No | Yes |

Platform-admin organization and global-dataset administration are separate operator capabilities. These customer guides do not grant them.

## Machine credentials

A scoped API key authorizes only its granted capabilities and resource restrictions. It does not sign a person in to the console, enable a hosted feature or provide a target model’s credentials. Existing Evals keys do not automatically gain hosted redteam rights.

[Create and configure an SDK key](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md) and [read team management](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/workspace/team-and-roles.md) for the actual controls.

## If a control is missing or disabled

1.  Confirm the organization and your current role.
2.  Read the page’s setup/readiness message.
3.  Check target approval and the selected project’s state.
4.  Ask an admin for the specific missing role or capability. Do not share an owner’s password or API token.

---

# Supported agent targets

> Choose an interface supported by the workflow you intend to run.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/reference/supported-targets/)

An approved connection defines how Martian reaches your agent. Registering a URL does not establish every workflow is compatible with it.

| Interface | Assessments | Dataset Evals | Main prerequisite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stateless HTTP chat | Supported | Supported | Validated, approved and active connection with chat authorization |
| Streamable HTTP MCP | Supported | Unsupported | Selected entry tool and approved argument/response contract |
| Public HTTPS browser chat | Supported, endpoint-only and serial | Unsupported | Compatible chat interface; public HTTPS on port 443 |
| Session-backed HTTP | Supported where the approved session contract applies | Unsupported | Approved session create/use/cleanup contract |
| Customer local callback through SDK | SDK redteam workflow | SDK prediction function | Correct SDK connection/scopes; target/provider credentials remain in your process |

## HTTP and MCP access

Normal customer endpoints require public HTTPS. Internal demo host allowlists and local-HTTP development settings are operator-owned exceptions; they are not a way to register an arbitrary private address from the customer console.

MCP validation discovers tools and binds approval to the selected schema. Revalidate after the contract, credentials or sandbox bindings change. A changed dynamic connection does not silently fall back to a legacy target.

## Browser chat

The browser executor supports the approved website flow and optional username/password website sign-in. URL validation checks URL/access configuration, not successful login. SSO, MFA, CAPTCHA, handoff and unsupported chat discovery can stop execution. Website sign-in is distinct from an attested synthetic business identity.

A reusable fresh conversation must also work after setup. The [recorded browser example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/assessments/evidence-and-results.md#read-a-browser-run-that-needs-attention) signed in and sent two neutral messages, then stopped with an uncertain action when fresh-conversation verification timed out. That observation does not qualify a completed browser assessment.

## Evals and saved outputs

A dataset run sends selected active inputs to its approved HTTP target. Saved-output scoring, reviews and comparisons use retained values; they do not resend the target request. Paid model judging requires its own readiness and acknowledgement.

**Next:** [Set up a connection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/agents/connections.md) or [use SDK callbacks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/redteam.md).

---

# Troubleshooting

> Resolve common access, connection, run, dataset and scoring failures safely.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/reference/troubleshooting/)

Start with the action’s recorded state and exact error. Refresh retained history before submitting duplicate work.

| Symptom | Check | Safe next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invitation is incomplete, expired or revoked | Correct recipient, organization address, latest link | Ask the inviter to replace it; keep links private |
| Sign-in works but a control is missing | Role and selected organization | Use the permissions table; ask for the specific required authority |
| Agent exists but cannot run | Draft/validation/approval/connection changes | Complete validation and approval; rotate/reapprove changed credentials |
| Browser URL validates but assessment fails | Website login, SSO/MFA/CAPTCHA/chat discovery | Inspect the run error; URL validation was not login success |
| Evals says setup is pending or needs review | Organization readiness, selected project | Use Refresh setup; ask an admin to resolve a failed/uncertain setup |
| A run is refused as busy | Organization-wide target/scoring admission | Wait for the active work; inspect its stop/final state |
| Launch response was lost | Existing saved run and launch request | Inspect/recover saved work before creating another request |
| Needs attention retains a submission error after refresh | Original run ID and runtime admission | Ask your operator to inspect that same campaign; a successful refresh response or an ended label does not prove downstream execution stopped |
| Dataset import is rejected | Preview row errors, fields, duplicate IDs, file format | Correct the entire upload; invalid input is not partially merged |
| Draft changed during publish | Current revision and validation hash | Refresh and review; publish the intended new revision |
| Published global dataset is read-only | Reserved martian: catalogue entry | Use Copy to my datasets, then edit your organization’s copy |
| Exact match is false unexpectedly | Complete actual/expected text | Check punctuation, extra prose and formatting; stripped case differences alone are ignored |
| Model judging unavailable | Model access, organization readiness, acknowledgement | Use supported code scoring or ask the admin; never invent missing feedback |
| Review saved but queue still pending | All required questions and native feedback verification | Wait/refresh; verify each latest required answer, not only the last clicked row |
| Export refuses too many results | Match count and active filters | Narrow the query; do not treat a partial page as the whole dataset |
| SDK exits with a setup error | Exact installed version, variables, scopes and supported command | Follow SDK configuration; martian scan is not the current supported CLI |

## Keep evidence useful

Record the run ID, approximate time, action, visible error and the steps already tried. Exclude passwords, tokens, cookies, customer prompts and private exports from shared issues. Use synthetic examples when reproducing a problem.

## Stop and uncertainty

A stop acknowledgement is not proof that an in-flight provider call has completed. Wait for final state and inspect retained work. Do not repeatedly retry an uncertain paid operation just to obtain a passing result.

**Next:** [Permissions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/permissions.md), [limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/limits.md) or the [SDK configuration guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md).

---

# Use these docs with an AI assistant

> Copy a complete page or share a public Markdown link that an assistant can read without signing in.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/reference/using-with-agents/)

Every documentation page has **Copy page** above its title. It copies the article as Markdown, including code examples, prerequisites, verification notices and screenshot links.

## Share a page

1.  Open the guide you need.
2.  Select **Copy page** and paste it into your assistant’s chat.
3.  To share a link instead, open the arrow beside **Copy page** and select **Copy agent link**. Paste the link into your chat and ask the assistant to read it.

The agent link opens a public, plain-text Markdown copy on GitHub. It needs no account, JavaScript or product access. This is an independent HTTPS access path alongside the documentation website. The content includes a link back to the web version.

**View Markdown** opens the same plain-text page. Use it if your browser blocks clipboard access, or if JavaScript is disabled. Select and copy its text manually.

## Give an assistant more context

-   [Agent index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/llms.txt): a list of pages with short descriptions and direct Markdown links. The page menu also links to this index.
-   [Complete documentation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/llms-full.txt): every page in one text file. It is larger; start with a specific guide when possible.

The site publishes the same files at `/markdown/<page-path>.md`, `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`. Each HTML page advertises its Markdown alternatives in its document head, so tools that inspect page metadata can discover them.

## Keep the guide’s limits in context

A copied page retains its role requirements, walkthrough qualification and links to the tested-version record. Ask the assistant to check those before suggesting a step. A partly verified guide still has unverified steps; a Markdown copy does not change that status. See [Verification and limitations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

These are public instructions. Sharing a page does not give an assistant access to your workspace, API keys or authenticated product. Supply only the context you intend to share.

# Guide verification record

> Review source revisions, real captures, completed checks and remaining gaps.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/reference/verification/)

These guides are being qualified against actual running application/backend states with synthetic data. A source review, an observed screen and a completed end-to-end run are recorded separately. A pending walkthrough is not a passed walkthrough.

## Current publication status

The site is being published iteratively. Guides with unfinished walkthroughs show a short notice above the instructions. Detailed roles, dates, tested environments and qualification records are collected here and retained in **Copy page** Markdown. Authenticated captures and complete execution checks are added as they pass.

Of **37 task guides**, **26 are verified**, **7 are partly verified** and **4 await walkthrough verification**. The screenshot record contains **142 captured references** across **130 unique PNGs**. These counts come from the current coverage and screenshot manifests.

The application supports desktop workflows. The documentation itself is also checked on narrow layouts. Screenshots are direct application captures; no functionality is invented with DOM edits or mocked API responses.

The public site now passes trusted HTTPS checks, including nested guides, Markdown, screenshots, diagrams and example downloads. HTTP and the earlier GitHub Pages address redirect to HTTPS. The GitHub Markdown mirror remains an independent access path for assistants. These publication checks are separate from the application walkthroughs below.

The latest completeness audit added the missing project dashboard, native annotation and network-observer instructions and a [console map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/console-navigation.md). The dashboard and annotation guides now have real console captures and successful walkthroughs in isolated QA. Network observation still awaits an authorized compatible source and privileged sensors. Earlier failed reads remain recorded; the successful checks below do not establish hosted-beta parity or general service reliability.

## SDK compatibility

The task guides install the latest SDK and keep release announcements in [PyPI release history](https://pypi.org/project/martian-sdk/#history). Verification remains tied to the releases actually exercised:

-   **SDK 0.1.2:** API-key management, persisted Evals, red teaming and combined CI were qualified against the recorded isolated services. The [combined CI receipt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/examples/validation/sdk-ci-0.1.2-2026-11-13.json) identifies the original tutorial snapshot and package hashes. Its original ZIP is historical; the current download uses an unpinned install.
-   **SDK 0.1.3:** installation, the account-free local preview, YAML validation, suite-file evaluations, deterministic checks, rubric/guidelines/conditions judges through one provider route, rejected-token handling and local evaluation storage were exercised. API-key management, persisted CI and hosted red teaming were not requalified on this release.

Installing a newer release does not extend those recorded results automatically. Validate your workflow before upgrading production CI, and record its selected dependency version in your lockfile.

## Availability distinctions

**Verified** means the recorded guide walkthrough passed against its named environment. **Source reviewed** means implementation was inspected but its live walkthrough remains pending. **Preview** describes a visible non-enforcing or otherwise limited capability. **Unsupported** means the current contract does not provide that operation. The guides preserve these boundaries.

The current Pipeline view explicitly labels its configuration as a preview: automated runs and waiver management are not connected. Its earlier illustrative command has been removed. Other limits include unsupported target interfaces for dataset Evals, a Threat Intel view without a live feed, and network containment that remains a preview. Use the supported SDK CLI and controls documented here.

# Gate CI on Evals and redteam

> Run evaluations and adversarial probes in one persisted CI session, verify its result, and retain safe reports.

Source: [Web version](https://docs.martiansecurity.ai/sdk/ci/)

> **Page qualification:** Python SDK · Scoped machine key; owner/admin issues key and publishes tutorial dataset · Verified 2026-11-13 · Named local QA for standalone probes and console persistence; GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04/Python 3.12 for exact public ZIP combined CLI on disposable pinned services. [Verification details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/reference/verification.md).

Run the Evals tests and one YAML redteam suite in a single pytest execution and retain one Backend CI session. A successful required gate needs complete test coverage, policy satisfaction, a valid persisted acknowledgment, and any explicitly required exports.

## Before you start

-   Use Python 3.12+ and **`martian-sdk[evals]`** from [installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md).
-   Complete the [published dataset setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/evaluations.md), [prepare redteam.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/redteam.md#1-inspect-the-one-probe-plan), and [validate it without a paid call](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/redteam.md#2-validate-without-a-paid-call). You do not need to execute a standalone redteam probe first; combined CI executes its own probe.
-   An owner/admin supplies a key with `evals:read`, `evals:write`, `ci:read`, `ci:write`, and `redteam:run`, with restrictions matching this dataset and agent. Hosted generation/judging must be enabled and configured for the organization.
-   Set `MARTIAN_API_URL`, `MARTIAN_API_TOKEN`, `MARTIAN_AGENT_ID`, and `MARTIAN_EVALS_GIT_SHA`. The agent must belong to the organization; the revision must identify the code tested.
-   Run trusted code. Keep platform and callback/provider secrets out of unreviewed pull-request code. Paid redteam/judge calls need your approved execution allowance.

## 1\. Check the complete suite

Run this guide from the **Git repository root prepared in the installation guide**, where the tutorial source has already been committed. Check the working directory before running commands:

```sh
pwd
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git status --short
```

The two directory paths should identify the same tutorial/customer repository. The complete runnable layout includes all of these files:

```text
demo_agent.py
pytest.ini
support-regressions.jsonl
redteam.yaml
redteam.py
key_agent_id.py
tests/evals/test_quality.py
tests/evals/test_dataset.py
combined_ci.py
github-actions.yml
```

`test_quality.py` records two inline exact-match checks. `test_dataset.py` pulls the published two-record **`docs-support-regressions`** dataset, runs the callback and asserts Backend-compatible exact match. `redteam.yaml` plans one gated prompt-leakage probe.

Keep the YAML redteam suite out of the pytest tests themselves: the combined runner adds it as a required test item. Including it a second time would repeat paid work.

Obtain `MARTIAN_AGENT_ID` with the installation guide’s [agent-bound key lookup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MorningHQ/martian-security-docs/main/public/markdown/sdk/install-and-configure.md#5-resolve-the-exact-ci-agent-uuid). The existing registration is attribution and an access binding; the callback under test is still the committed local `demo_agent.answer` function.

## 2\. Validate the configuration

```sh
git status --short
export MARTIAN_EVALS_GIT_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
```
